normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the coined unit, the rebuilding verb and the four neighbouring practices.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用新造的单位、表示重建的动词，以及四种相邻做法。

normal.en: Ecosystem is a household of parts, and restoration means rebuilding, so the phrase is rebuilding a household of parts.
normal.cn: 前半是部件组成的家，后半是重建，所以这个短语就是重建一个部件之家。

normal.en: Restore, restoration and restorative share one Latin verb for renewing.
normal.cn: 「恢复」「恢复」与「有恢复作用的」共用一个表示更新的拉丁动词。

normal.en: Remediation cleans, rehabilitation repairs function, restoration rebuilds structure and species.
normal.cn: 污染治理做清洁，修复修功能，恢复重建结构与物种。

normal.en: The reference site is the picture of what the work is aiming at.
normal.cn: 参照地点就是这项工作所想达到的那幅画。

normal.en: Decades are the normal unit, because a rebuilt system has to assemble itself.
normal.cn: 数十年是常规单位，因为重建的系统必须自行组合。

abstract.en: Restoration is not a return to a past state but the construction of a system that can continue without us.
abstract.cn: 恢复不是回到某个过去的状态，而是造出一个能离开我们继续运转的系统。

abstract.en: A reference site is a memory made visible, and every restoration is an argument about which memory to trust.
abstract.cn: 参照地点是被看见的记忆，每一次恢复都是关于该信哪段记忆的争论。

abstract.en: The work succeeds when the workers become unnecessary, which is a strange kind of success.
abstract.cn: 当工作者变得多余时，这项工作才算成功，这是一种奇怪的成功。

examples.en: Ecosystem restoration on the floodplain reduced erosion within four years.
examples.cn: 漫滩上的生态系统恢复在四年内减少了侵蚀。

examples.en: The fund pays for ecosystem restoration in the upper catchment.
examples.cn: 这笔基金为上游流域的生态系统恢复出资。

examples.en: Students compared two methods of ecosystem restoration on the same slope.
examples.cn: 学生们在同一片坡地上比较了两种生态系统恢复方法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「伊扣西斯特姆 瑞斯托瑞申」——前面是生态系统，后面是重新立起来，把塌掉的系统重新立起来

root: 希腊语 oikos「家宅」+ 希腊语 systema「有机整体」→ 表示「生态系统」的新词，一九三五年由坦斯利造出；拉丁语 restaurare「重建、更新」← re-「再次」+ 词干「站立」→ 经法语 restoratio 进入英语为表示「恢复」的名词。两词在二十世纪后期合为生态学术语，确切首见年代只能给约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses separate the aim from the means: recovery as work, intervention, a reference state, a science, a programme, the neighbouring practices, results, people and time.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把目标与手段分开：作为工作的恢复、干预、参照状态、学科、计划、相邻做法、成效、人与时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a logged slope fenced off, replanted with local trees, its stream running clear again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片被砍过的山坡被围起来，补种本地树苗，溪水重新变清。

branches.en: THE AIM AND THE MEANS: helping recovery, and the intervention that distinguishes it from neglect.
branches.cn: 目标与手段：协助恢复，以及使它区别于放任的干预。

branches.en: THE PICTURE: a reference site that says what recovery should look like.
branches.cn: 图景：一个说明恢复应长什么样的参照地点。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: a science with methods, and a programme with targets and money.
branches.cn: 制度：有方法的学科，以及有目标与资金的计划。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: narrower practices that clean or repair without rebuilding.
branches.cn: 边界：只做清洁或修复、不重建的较窄做法。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE AND THE PEOPLE: measured returns, shared long-term care, and a horizon in decades.
branches.cn: 证据与人：可测的回归、共同承担的长期维护，以及以数十年计的视野。

intro.en: A Greek house and whole make the unit; a Latin again and standing stem make the rebuilding.
intro.cn: 希腊语的「家宅」与「整体」构成单位，拉丁语的「再次」与「站立」词干构成重建。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies restaurare and its noun restoratio, both recorded; the deeper standing stem is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「重建」动词与其名词，两者皆有记录；更早的「站立」词干属重构形式。

items.example: It marks the whole place where life is carried on.
items.exampleCN: 它标记生命在其中展开的整个场所。

items.example: It marks the unit as a working whole.
items.exampleCN: 它标记这个单位是运转的整体。

items.example: It marks doing the work a second time.
items.exampleCN: 它标记把这件事再做一遍。

items.example: It supplies the image of something set upright again.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「重新立起来」的形象。

items.example: It is the recorded direct source.
items.exampleCN: 它是有记录的直接来源。

items.example: It makes the noun for the work.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示这项工作的名词。

items.example: It makes the adjective for what restores.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「有恢复作用」的形容词。

items.example: It is the recorded Greek source of the first element.
items.exampleCN: 它是有记录的、第一成分的希腊语来源。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语动词经法语进入英语，义为「恢复；修复」
由该动词加动作名词词尾构成，义为「恢复」
由该词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「有恢复作用的」
由该名词与生态学组合而成，义为「恢复生态学」

definition_zh: 受威胁的；受到危害的；（物种）面临灭绝风险的
definition_en: put in danger by something, or, of a species, facing a high risk of extinction in the wild
core_image: 一片不断缩小的岩壁草坡，几条新修的牧道把它切成碎块，兽群只能挤在剩下的一小片岩脊上
scene: 新修的牧道把最后一片草坡切成碎块，兽群只能挤在剩下的岩脊上。The report lists the snow leopard as threatened across most of its range.
sceneCN: 这里指物种面临灭绝风险，属于保护的受威胁总称（第 1 个义项：面临灭绝风险的物种）；句意为报告把雪豹在其大部分分布区内列为受威胁物种。

pos.zh: 受威胁的；受到危害的
（物种）面临灭绝风险的，涵盖易危、濒危与极危

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词去掉词尾还原的动词，义为「威胁；危及」
由动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「威胁的；险恶的」
该词族的基座名词，义为「威胁；危险」
由该形容词与「物种」组合而成，义为「受威胁物种」，法律与保护文本的固定术语
由表示否定的前缀加该词构成，义为「未受威胁的」
由表示否定的前缀加该词构成，义为「非受威胁的」，用于名录分类

senses.title: Facing a high risk of extinction
senses.definition: facing a high risk of extinction in the wild, the umbrella reading of the term in conservation
senses.definitionCN: 在野外面临较高的灭绝风险，是保护工作中这个术语的总括读法
senses.example: The orchid is threatened because its only pollinator has vanished.
senses.exampleCN: 这种兰花之所以受威胁，是因为它唯一的传粉者已经消失。
senses.why: The word is the past participle of a verb meaning to menace, so a threatened species is one under menace.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是意为「威胁」的动词的过去分词，因此受威胁物种就是处在威胁之下的物种。

senses.title: The umbrella of three red-list categories
senses.titleCN: 红色名录三个等级的统称
senses.definition: the collective label for the categories vulnerable, endangered and critically endangered
senses.definitionCN: 对易危、濒危、极危三个等级的统称
senses.example: Under the red-list scheme, threatened covers three categories, not one.
senses.exampleCN: 按红色名录的划分，受威胁涵盖三个等级，而不是一个。
senses.why: A single word was needed for the group, so the broadest label was placed above the three narrower ones.
senses.whyCN: 这一组需要一个统称，于是最宽的标签被放在三个较窄等级之上。

senses.title: Under pressure from a named cause
senses.titleCN: 受到某一具体原因的压迫
senses.definition: placed under pressure by a specific cause such as drainage, logging, fishing or climate change
senses.definitionCN: 因排水、伐木、捕捞或气候变化等具体原因而承受压力
senses.example: The fen is threatened by the pumping station upstream.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沼泽正受到上游泵站的威胁。
senses.why: The passive form keeps the cause in view: something is doing the menacing.
senses.whyCN: 被动形式把原因留在视野里：总有某个东西在施加威胁。

senses.title: Legally listed and protected
senses.definition: entered on a statutory list that triggers protection, permits and recovery plans
senses.definitionCN: 被列入法定名录，从而触发保护、许可与恢复计划
senses.example: Once the fish was listed as threatened, the dam licence was reviewed.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鱼一旦被列为受威胁，大坝许可就被重新审查。
senses.why: A list is where a category becomes an obligation, so protection follows the name onto paper.
senses.whyCN: 名录是等级变成义务的地方，因此保护跟着名字落到纸上。

senses.title: Applied to habitats and systems
senses.definition: used of places, ecosystems or processes that are likely to be lost or degraded
senses.definitionCN: 用于可能丧失或退化的地点、生态系统或过程
senses.example: The threatened floodplain forest is now part of the reserve.
senses.exampleCN: 受威胁的漫滩森林现在已纳入保护区。
senses.why: The adjective needs no living subject, so it transfers to the ground, the system and the process that support species.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词不要求主语是生物，因此可以转到支撑物种的地面、系统与过程上。

senses.title: At risk of being lost, in general use
senses.definition: in everyday speech, likely to disappear, fail or be damaged
senses.definitionCN: 在日常语言中，指可能消失、失败或受损
senses.example: The village school is threatened with closure next year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所村校面临明年关闭的威胁。
senses.why: Before it was a conservation term it was an everyday participle, and ordinary things can still be threatened.
senses.whyCN: 在成为保护术语之前，它只是日常分词，普通事物依然可以被威胁。

senses.title: The fixed phrase with extinction
senses.titleCN: 与「灭绝」构成的固定搭配
senses.definition: appearing in the set phrase threatened with extinction, the standard wording of reports
senses.definitionCN: 出现在「面临灭绝」这一固定说法中，是报告的标准措辞
senses.example: One in eight plant species is threatened with extinction.
senses.exampleCN: 八分之一的植物物种面临灭绝。
senses.why: Reports need fixed wording, and the phrase with extinction became the standard frame for the number.
senses.whyCN: 报告需要固定措辞，与「灭绝」搭配的说法成了承载数字的标准框架。

senses.title: A wider reading below endangered
senses.titleCN: 与「濒危」相比更宽的一档
senses.definition: used more broadly than endangered, which is one narrower category inside it
senses.definitionCN: 比「濒危」用得更宽，「濒危」只是它内部较窄的一个等级
senses.example: A vulnerable species is threatened, but not every threatened species is endangered.
senses.exampleCN: 易危物种属于受威胁，但并非每个受威胁物种都是濒危。
senses.why: One label covers three ranks, so the wider word and the narrower word cannot be used as equals.
senses.whyCN: 一个标签覆盖三个等级，因此宽词与窄词不能当作同级词使用。

senses.title: The passive sense of being menaced
senses.titleCN: 被施加威胁的被动意义
senses.definition: the plain participial sense of being warned or menaced by a person or force
senses.definitionCN: 表示被人或力量警告、胁迫的普通分词意义
senses.example: He felt threatened by the crowd at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 门口的人群让他感到受到威胁。
senses.why: Long before red lists, the participle described how a person feels under menace, and that sense never left.
senses.whyCN: 在红色名录出现之前很久，这个分词就描述人在威胁之下是什么感受，那一层意义从未离开。

intro.en: The word is native English, not Latin. An Old English noun for pressure or a crowd produced a verb, and its past participle became the adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，不是拉丁语借词：古英语中表示压力或人群的名词生出动词，其过去分词成为形容词。

items.en: The noun meant a crowd, pressure or oppression, and it named force applied to someone.
items.cn: 这个名词意为人群、压力或压迫，指施加于人的力量。

items.en: The verb formed on that noun meant to menace or to press someone with threats.
items.cn: 由该名词构成的动词意为威胁，或以威胁逼迫某人。

items.en: The spelling and vowels shifted, and the verb spread from personal menace to danger of any kind.
items.cn: 拼写与元音发生变化，这个动词的用法从针对人的威胁扩展到任何危险。

items.en: The past participle in -ed became an adjective meaning placed under menace.
items.cn: 带过去分词词尾的形式成为形容词，意为「被置于威胁之下」。

items.en: Red data books and then the red list gave the adjective a technical sense as an umbrella category.
items.cn: 红色数据手册与后来的红色名录赋予这个形容词一个技术义，作为等级统称。

note.en: The first group shares the threat stem; the second group names the conservation ranks and the neighbouring states.
note.cn: 第一组共用「威胁」词干；第二组是保护等级与相邻状态的名称。

entries.definition: The verb: to menace or put at risk.
entries.definitionCN: 动词：威胁或使处于危险。

entries.definition: Menacing, or likely to cause harm.
entries.definitionCN: 指威胁性的，或可能造成损害的。

entries.definition: The base noun: a warning of harm or a source of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 基座名词：伤害的警告或危险的来源。

entries.definition: The adjective itself; note the single syllable ending in the past participle.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词本身；注意其过去分词词尾构成的单音节收尾。

entries.definition: A strand of fibre; it looks and sounds close but belongs to a spinning word.
entries.definitionCN: 指纤维细线；形音相近，但属于纺织词。

entries.definition: A narrower red-list category, and in loose use a synonym for at risk.
entries.definitionCN: 是较窄的红色名录等级，宽松用法中与「有风险」同义。

entries.definition: The lowest of the three threatened categories, one step below endangered.
entries.definitionCN: 是三个受威胁等级中最低的一档，比濒危低一级。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for exposure to possible harm.
entries.definitionCN: 指暴露于可能伤害之下的普通说法。

entries.definition: In danger, a more literary synonym common in American conservation writing.
entries.definitionCN: 指处于危险中，是更书面化的同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Old English pressure noun, the participle ending and the three red-list categories.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用古英语的「压力」名词、过去分词词尾与红色名录的三个等级。

normal.en: The Old English noun meant pressure, so a threatened thing is something pressed.
normal.cn: 古英语名词意为压力，所以受威胁的东西就是被压着的东西。

normal.en: Threat, threaten, threatening and threatened are one family with four jobs.
normal.cn: 「威胁」名词、动词、现在分词与过去分词是一家四口，各司一职。

normal.en: Red lists use threatened as an umbrella over vulnerable, endangered and critically endangered.
normal.cn: 红色名录把受威胁作为易危、濒危、极危之上的统称。

normal.en: Threatened with extinction is the fixed phrase that appears in almost every report.
normal.cn: 「面临灭绝」是几乎每份报告都会用的固定说法。

normal.en: Threatened is broader than endangered, the way a roof is broader than its ridge.
normal.cn: 受威胁比濒危更宽，就像屋顶比屋脊更宽。

abstract.en: A threatened species is a story that has been cut down to its last few pages.
abstract.cn: 受威胁物种是一个被删到只剩最后几页的故事。

abstract.en: Threat is pressure applied from outside, which is why the word is passive: the species is acted upon.
abstract.cn: 威胁是从外部施加的压力，所以这个词是被动的：物种是被作用的一方。

abstract.en: Every category on the list is a prediction, and predictions can be revised but not undone.
abstract.cn: 名录上的每一个等级都是预测，预测可以修订，却无法撤销。

examples.en: The bird is threatened by the drainage of its last marsh.
examples.cn: 这种鸟受到其最后一片沼泽被排干的威胁。

examples.en: Threatened species receive extra protection under the act.
examples.cn: 受威胁物种依据该法获得额外保护。

examples.en: Three of the threatened plants survive only on this ridge.
examples.cn: 这些受威胁植物中有三种只在这条山脊上存活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「斯瑞特恩德」——斯瑞特是压过来的威胁，恩德是被压着，被威胁压着的，就是受威胁的

root: 古英语 þreat「人群、压力、压迫」→ þreatnian「威胁、逼迫」→ 中古英语的动词形式 → 现代英语中表示「威胁」的动词，其过去分词 由「被施加威胁」转为形容词「受威胁的」。保护领域的统称用法由二十世纪红色数据手册与红色名录确立。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses start from the passive idea of being pressed, then move through the red-list umbrella, the named cause, legal listing, habitats, general use and the fixed phrase.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从「被压着」这一被动意思出发，经红色名录统称、具体原因、法律名录、生境、一般用法与固定说法展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shrinking grass ridge cut into pieces by new tracks, the herd pressed onto what is left.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片被新路切成碎块、不断缩小的草坡岩脊，兽群被挤在剩下的一小块上。

branches.en: THE PLAIN PRESSURE: a named cause on one side, and the passive feeling of menace on the other.
branches.cn: 朴素压力：一边是具体原因，一边是被威胁的感受。

branches.en: THE SPECIES: a living thing facing a high risk of extinction.
branches.cn: 物种：面临高灭绝风险的生物。

branches.en: THE UMBRELLA: three red-list categories, broader than endangered alone.
branches.cn: 统称：三个红色名录等级，比单说濒危更宽。

branches.en: THE EXTENSION: habitats and systems, and everyday things at risk of being lost.
branches.cn: 延伸：生境与系统，以及日常事物面临丧失。

branches.en: THE CONSEQUENCE: legal listing, and the fixed phrase used in reports.
branches.cn: 后果：法律名录，以及报告中使用的固定说法。

intro.en: The word is native English and grew from a noun, so its affixes belong to English rather than to Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，从名词生长出来，因此其构词成分属于英语而非拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin relative of this family, so the Latin entries are left empty rather than filled with approximations.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族没有拉丁语同族词，因此拉丁语词条留空，而不是用近似形式填充。

items.example: It supplies the original image of force applied.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「施加力量」的原始形象。

items.meaning: to menace, to press with threats
items.example: It is the recorded source of the modern verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是现代动词有记录的来源。

items.example: It turned the noun into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词变成动词。

items.example: It turned the verb into the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成形容词。

items.example: It makes the active counterpart.
items.exampleCN: 它构成主动的那一面。

items.example: It is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个词族的基座。

items.example: It marks a species not on the list.
items.exampleCN: 它标记不在名录上的物种。

items.example: It marks the negative class in listings.
items.exampleCN: 它标记名录中的否定类别。

derivatives.zh: 由古英语名词加动词词尾构成，义为「威胁」
由该动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「威胁性的」
该词族的基座名词，义为「威胁」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「未受威胁的」

definition_zh: 易危物种；被评定为野外灭绝风险较高的一档物种
definition_en: a species assessed as facing a high risk of extinction in the wild, the lowest of the three threatened categories
core_image: 一小群鸟只在一条窄窄的河滩上筑巢，滩上每一处卵石都挨得很近，河岸外侧就是工地
scene: 这条河滩只剩一小段还能筑巢，外围已经开始施工，鸟群被挤在卵石最密的那一块。The bird is now listed as a vulnerable species after the survey.
sceneCN: 这里指按保护等级评定为易危的物种，属于受威胁三档中最低的一档（第 1 个义项：易危等级物种）；句意为调查之后这种鸟被列为易危物种。

pos.zh: 易危物种（保护等级术语）
脆弱的物种（一般描述性用法）

derivatives.zh: 该短语的限定词，由拉丁语表示「伤口」的词派生，义为「易受伤害的；脆弱的」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「脆弱性；易受损害性」
由该形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「脆弱地」
由表示否定的前缀加该形容词构成，义为「不会受伤害的」
相邻等级术语，由表示「使陷于危险」的分词与「物种」构成，义为「濒危物种」
最高一档的相邻术语，义为「极危物种」

senses.title: The red-list category of vulnerable
senses.titleCN: 红色名录中的易危等级
senses.definition: a species assessed against published criteria as facing a high risk of extinction in the wild
senses.definitionCN: 按已公布标准评定为在野外面临较高灭绝风险的物种
senses.example: The frog qualifies as a vulnerable species because its single pond is shrinking.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蛙之所以属于易危物种，是因为它唯一的那片池塘正在缩小。
senses.why: The category sits between near threatened and endangered, so the phrase names a rank rather than a mood.
senses.whyCN: 这一档位于近危与濒危之间，因此这个短语命名的是一个等级，而不是一种心情。

senses.title: The criteria that decide the rank
senses.definition: a species meeting thresholds for population decline, small range, small numbers or measured extinction probability
senses.definitionCN: 达到种群下降、分布狭窄、数量稀少或测得灭绝概率等阈值的物种
senses.example: A decline of thirty per cent over ten years can make it a vulnerable species.
senses.exampleCN: 十年内下降三成，就可能使它成为易危物种。
senses.why: A rank without numbers would be an opinion, so published thresholds were written to decide the label.
senses.whyCN: 没有数值的等级只是一种意见，因此公布了阈值来决定这个标签。

senses.title: A broader legal reading
senses.titleCN: 法律文本中较宽的用法
senses.definition: in some statutes, any listed species at risk, not strictly the red-list rank
senses.definitionCN: 在有些法规中，泛指任何被列入名录的受风险物种，而不严格限于红色名录等级
senses.example: The act protects vulnerable species without defining the term by red-list numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 该法保护易危物种，却没有用红色名录的数值来定义它。
senses.why: Statutes need words that lawyers can apply, so the term is sometimes loosened beyond its scientific rank.
senses.whyCN: 法规需要律师能直接适用的词，因此这个术语有时会被放宽到超出其科学等级。

senses.title: One step below endangered
senses.definition: the lowest of the three threatened categories, moving next to endangered if conditions worsen
senses.definitionCN: 三个受威胁等级中最低的一档，条件恶化时下一档即为濒危
senses.example: A vulnerable species becomes endangered when the decline continues.
senses.exampleCN: 如果下降持续，一个易危物种就会变成濒危物种。
senses.why: Ranks are thresholds on one line, so crossing the next threshold simply renames the same species.
senses.whyCN: 等级是同一条线上的阈值，越过下一个阈值只是给同一个物种换个名称。

senses.title: Vulnerable to a named pressure
senses.definition: exposed to a specific threat such as disease, drought, bycatch or warming water
senses.definitionCN: 暴露于疾病、干旱、误捕或水温升高等具体威胁之下
senses.example: Island birds are a vulnerable species group wherever rats arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 只要有鼠类进入，海岛鸟类就是一整类易危物种。
senses.why: A rank can also be earned by exposure rather than numbers, when one pressure is known to hit the whole group.
senses.whyCN: 等级也可以由暴露程度而非数值换来，当某种压力已知会打击整个类群时就是如此。

senses.title: A listing that triggers action
senses.definition: a status that brings recovery plans, permits and funding with it
senses.definitionCN: 带来恢复计划、许可与资金的身份
senses.example: Once named a vulnerable species, the plant got a recovery plan.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物一旦被列为易危物种，就获得了恢复计划。
senses.why: A name on a list releases money that a name off the list cannot, so the label has practical force.
senses.whyCN: 名字在名录上能放出不在名录上放不出的钱，因此这个标签有实际力量。

senses.title: A label blurred in the media
senses.titleCN: 媒体中含义模糊的标签
senses.definition: used loosely in news for any declining species, sometimes confused with endangered
senses.definitionCN: 新闻中宽松地用于任何数量下降的物种，有时与「濒危」混用
senses.example: Headlines called it a vulnerable species long before the assessment was finished.
senses.exampleCN: 评估尚未结束，标题就已称它为易危物种。
senses.why: Journalists borrow technical names before the paperwork is done, and the borrowing blurs the ranks.
senses.whyCN: 记者往往在文书完成前就借用技术名称，这种借用把等级弄混了。

senses.title: The contrast with threatened as a whole
senses.titleCN: 与「受威胁」总称的层次关系
senses.definition: one category inside the threatened umbrella, so every vulnerable species is threatened but not the reverse
senses.definitionCN: 受威胁统称之内的一个等级，因此每个易危物种都属于受威胁，反之不成立
senses.example: The briefing confused a vulnerable species with any threatened one.
senses.exampleCN: 这份简报把易危物种与任何受威胁物种混为一谈。
senses.why: A part and its whole share a word in casual use, and the hierarchy has to be stated to be kept.
senses.whyCN: 部分与整体在随意使用中会共用一个词，要保住层级就必须把它讲明白。

senses.title: A descriptively fragile species
senses.titleCN: 描述意义上的脆弱物种
senses.definition: in ordinary writing, a species easily harmed because it is few, specialised or slow to reproduce
senses.definitionCN: 在普通写作中，指因数量少、特化强或繁殖慢而容易受损的物种
senses.example: A large, slow-breeding mammal is a vulnerable species in any fragmented forest.
senses.exampleCN: 在任何破碎化的森林里，体型大、繁殖慢的兽类都是脆弱物种。
senses.why: Outside the list the adjective still works descriptively, naming the traits that make harm likely.
senses.whyCN: 在名录之外，这个形容词仍有描述作用，指出使伤害容易发生的那些特征。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin adjective meaning woundable to a Latin noun for kind or appearance. The conservation rank was fixed in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语中意为「易受伤」的形容词，接上一个意为「种类、外形」的拉丁名词。保护等级用法在二十世纪固定下来。

items.en: Vulnus meant a wound, and its stem supplied the idea of being open to injury.
items.cn: 这个词意为伤口，其词干提供了「容易受伤」的意思。

items.en: The verb meant to wound, and the adjective built on it described what can be wounded.
items.cn: 这个动词意为使受伤，由其构成的形容词描述可被伤害的东西。

items.en: The adjective meant woundable or open to injury, and English took it through French.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为易受伤的、会受伤害的，英语经法语借入。

items.en: Species meant appearance, form or kind, and it became the biological word for a kind of organism.
items.cn: 这个词意为外观、形态或种类，后来成为表示一类生物的生物学术语。

items.en: English first used vulnerable for places open to attack, and only later for bodies and animals.
items.cn: 英语最初用这个词指易受攻击的地点，后来才用于身体与动物。

items.en: The red list adopted vulnerable as the name of its lowest threatened category, with published numeric criteria.
items.cn: 红色名录采用「易危」作为受威胁三档中最低一档的名称，并公布了数值标准。

note.en: The first group shares vulnerable or species; the second group places the rank among its neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组共用 vulnerable 或 species；第二组把这个等级放进相邻等级之间。

entries.definition: Open to harm, physically or otherwise, the core adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指易受伤害，身体或其他方面皆可，是核心形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being open to harm; also a formal assessment category.
entries.definitionCN: 指易受伤害的状态，也是一种正式评估类别。

entries.definition: Not able to be harmed, the negated form.
entries.definitionCN: 指不会受伤害，是加否定前缀的形式。

entries.definition: A kind of organism; singular and plural are spelled alike.
entries.definitionCN: 指一类生物；单复数拼写相同。

entries.definition: A single example used for study, from the same looking stem.
entries.definitionCN: 指供研究用的单个标本，出自同一「观看」词干。

entries.definition: The next category up, facing a very high risk of extinction.
entries.definitionCN: 指高一档的等级，面临很高的灭绝风险。

entries.definition: The highest threatened category, facing an extremely high risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指最高的受威胁等级，面临极高的风险。

entries.definition: The category just below vulnerable, close to qualifying.
entries.definitionCN: 指刚好低于易危的一档，接近达标。

entries.definition: The umbrella over vulnerable, endangered and critically endangered.
entries.definitionCN: 指覆盖易危、濒危与极危的统称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin wound, the red-list ladder and the media confusion.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语「伤口」、红色名录的阶梯与媒体的混用。

normal.en: Vulnus is a wound, so a vulnerable species is one with its guard down.
normal.cn: 词根意为伤口，所以易危物种就是放下了防备的那一种。

normal.en: The ladder runs near threatened, vulnerable, endangered, critically endangered.
normal.cn: 阶梯是近危、易危、濒危、极危。

normal.en: Species is spelled the same in singular and plural, which catches many readers.
normal.cn: 「物种」一词单复数同形，这一点常让读者出错。

normal.en: Every vulnerable species is threatened, but not every threatened species is vulnerable.
normal.cn: 每个易危物种都属受威胁，但不是每个受威胁物种都属易危。

normal.en: Numbers decide the rank: decline rate, range size, population size and extinction probability.
normal.cn: 等级由数值决定：下降速率、分布面积、种群数量与灭绝概率。

abstract.en: Vulnerability is a measurement of nearness to absence, not a description of weakness.
abstract.cn: 易危是对「接近消失」的度量，而不是对虚弱的描述。

abstract.en: A rank is a promise about the future that a list makes on behalf of a species that cannot speak.
abstract.cn: 等级是名录替一个无法开口的物种对将来作出的承诺。

abstract.en: The same creature can be fragile in one landscape and ordinary in another, so the label belongs to a place as much as to a kind.
abstract.cn: 同一种生物在一片景观里脆弱，在另一片里平常，因此这个标签一半属于地点，一半属于物种。

examples.en: The survey recommended that the butterfly be listed as a vulnerable species.
examples.cn: 这项调查建议把这种蝴蝶列为易危物种。

examples.en: A vulnerable species can move to endangered within one generation.
examples.cn: 一个易危物种可能在一代之内转为濒危。

examples.en: Fishing pressure turned a common fish into a vulnerable species in a decade.
examples.cn: 捕捞压力在十年内把一种常见鱼变成了易危物种。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「卧尔纳若波 斯比西兹」——前半是容易受伤，后半是种类，容易受伤的种类就是易危物种

root: 拉丁语 vulnus「伤口」→ vulnerare「使受伤」→ 晚期拉丁语 vulnerabilis「易受伤的」，经法语进入英语；拉丁语 species「外观、种类」← specere「看」。保护等级「易危」由二十世纪红色名录确立，并配有公布的数量标准。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses hold one rank steady while changing the angle: the category, its criteria, its legal breadth, its place on the ladder, its pressures, its consequences and its loose public use.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项守住同一个等级，只换角度看：等级本身、评定标准、法律宽度、阶梯位置、所受压力、带来的后果与公众的宽松用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small flock nesting on one narrow shingle bank, with construction starting just beyond it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小群鸟在一条窄窄的卵石滩上筑巢，工地就在滩外开工。

branches.en: THE TWO READINGS: a fragile kind in ordinary speech, and a fixed category in assessment.
branches.cn: 两种读法：日常语言中的脆弱种类，与评估中的固定等级。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: decline rate, range, population size and extinction probability.
branches.cn: 数值：下降速率、分布面积、种群数量与灭绝概率。

branches.en: THE PLACE ON THE LADDER: one step below endangered, inside the threatened umbrella.
branches.cn: 阶梯位置：比濒危低一档，位于受威胁统称之内。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE: disease, drought, bycatch or warming water acting on the species.
branches.cn: 压力：疾病、干旱、误捕或水温升高作用于该物种。

branches.en: THE CONSEQUENCE AND THE NOISE: a recovery plan, a blurred headline, and a rank confused with the umbrella.
branches.cn: 后果与噪音：恢复计划、含义模糊的标题，以及被与统称混淆的等级。

intro.en: A Latin wound stem supplies the adjective and a Latin looking stem supplies the noun.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「伤口」词干提供形容词，拉丁语的「观看」词干提供名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vulnus, vulnerare, vulnerabilis and species, all recorded forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「伤口」「使受伤」「易受伤的」与「种类」四种有记录的形式。

items.example: It supplies the whole idea of exposure to injury.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「暴露于伤害」的整个意思。

items.example: It is the verb behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是形容词背后的动词。

items.example: It is the recorded source of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语形容词有记录的来源。

items.example: It marks the capacity to be wounded.
items.exampleCN: 它标记「能被伤害」这一能力。

items.example: It makes the noun of the state.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示该状态的名词。

items.example: It names the kind of organism.
items.exampleCN: 它命名生物的种类。

items.example: It is the stem behind the noun for kind.
items.exampleCN: 它是「种类」名词背后的词干。

items.example: It negates the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它否定这个形容词。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「脆弱性」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「不会受伤害的」
由该形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「脆弱地」
相邻等级术语，义为「濒危物种」

definition_zh: 入侵性的；（物种）外来的、迅速扩散并造成损害的；侵入性的；（肿瘤）侵袭性的；侵犯的
definition_en: spreading into a place or body where it does not belong, especially of a species that spreads beyond its native range and causes harm
core_image: 一条堤岸被外来的藤蔓整片盖住，本地芦苇从下面透不出一片叶子，藤尖还在向水面探
scene: 外来的藤蔓沿着堤岸一路铺开，本地芦苇被压在下面几乎见不到光。Managers call the vine invasive because it smothers the native reeds.
sceneCN: 这里指外来物种迅速扩散并造成损害（第 1 个义项：侵入并扩散造成危害）；句意为管理者称这种藤为入侵性的，因为它把本地芦苇压死。

pos.zh: 入侵性的；外来的并造成损害的
侵入性的；侵袭性的（医学）
侵犯的；侵扰的

derivatives.zh: 该词的基座动词，由表示「进入」的前缀加表示「走」的词干构成，义为「侵入；侵袭」
由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「入侵；侵袭」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「入侵者」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「入侵性；侵袭性」
由表示否定的前缀加该词构成，义为「非侵入性的」
由表示「最低限度」的副词与形容词构成，义为「微创的」

senses.title: Spreading beyond the native range and causing harm
senses.titleCN: 越出原生范围扩散并造成损害
senses.definition: of a species, spreading rapidly outside the range it evolved in and damaging the systems it enters
senses.definitionCN: 指物种在其演化范围之外迅速扩散，并损害它进入的系统
senses.example: The shrimp proved invasive in every estuary where it was released.
senses.exampleCN: 这种虾在每一个被放归的河口都表现出入侵性。
senses.why: The word pictures an entry by force, and ecology borrowed it for species that take ground rather than share it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词画出「强行进入」的画面，生态学借它来形容那些夺取地面而非共享地面的物种。

senses.title: Not every introduced species is invasive
senses.titleCN: 并非所有引入物种都是入侵性的
senses.definition: describing harm and spread, not mere foreign origin, so a naturalised species that stays put is not called invasive
senses.definitionCN: 描述损害与扩散，而不是单纯的外来出身，因此安分定居的归化物种不被称为入侵性
senses.example: The poppy is introduced here but not invasive; it has stayed in the same fields for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这种罂粟在这里是引入种，却不是入侵性的；它在一个世纪里都待在同一片田里。
senses.why: Origin and behaviour are separate tests, and the word marks the second one.
senses.whyCN: 出身与行为是两套检验，这个词标记的是第二套。

senses.title: Entering the body in medical procedures
senses.definition: of a procedure or device, entering the body by puncture, incision or tube
senses.definitionCN: 指操作或器械以穿刺、切开或插管的方式进入体内
senses.example: The clinic replaced the open operation with a less invasive test.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把开刀手术换成了侵入性更小的检查。
senses.why: Medicine kept the physical sense of going in, and it measures how far the entry goes.
senses.whyCN: 医学保留了「进入」的字面意义，并衡量进入的程度。

senses.title: Spreading into surrounding tissue
senses.definition: of a tumour or infection, growing into nearby tissue rather than staying contained
senses.definitionCN: 指肿瘤或感染向邻近组织生长，而不是局限在原处
senses.example: The scan showed an invasive growth that had crossed the wall of the duct.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示有一处已穿过管壁的侵袭性生长。
senses.why: Cancer that crosses a boundary is doing exactly what the Latin verb described: going in.
senses.whyCN: 越过边界的癌所做的正是那个拉丁动词所描述的：走进去。

senses.title: Intruding on privacy or rights
senses.definition: of a measure, technology or question, forcing its way into matters that should stay private
senses.definitionCN: 指措施、技术或提问强行进入本应私密的领域
senses.example: Staff called the new monitoring invasive and refused the ankle tags.
senses.exampleCN: 员工称新的监控侵犯个人，拒绝佩戴脚环。
senses.why: The metaphor needs no translation here: a boundary is crossed against the will of the person inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻在这里无需翻译：边界是在里面那个人不情愿的情况下被越过的。

senses.title: Spreading vigorously, of plants
senses.definition: of a plant, growing and spreading so strongly that it displaces others
senses.definitionCN: 指植物生长扩散极强，以致挤走其他植物
senses.example: The reed is invasive in the marsh and has taken most of the open water.
senses.exampleCN: 这种芦苇在沼泽里扩散极强，已经占去了大部分明水。
senses.why: A plant that takes open water is behaving like an army taking ground, which is why the military word transferred.
senses.whyCN: 占据明水的植物，其行为像一支夺取地面的军队，这就是军事词会转过来的原因。

senses.title: Of military entry by force
senses.definition: of a force or operation, entering another territory by armed force
senses.definitionCN: 指力量或行动以武力进入他国领土
senses.example: The history course compared invasive campaigns across two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这门历史课比较了两个世纪里的入侵性军事行动。
senses.why: The oldest sense is literal armed entry, and it remains available whenever a border is crossed by force.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是字面上的武装进入，只要边界被武力越过，这一义仍然可用。

senses.title: Of technologies that spread into new domains
senses.definition: of a tool or practice, spreading into areas where it was not expected and changing them
senses.definitionCN: 指工具或做法扩散到原本不被期待的领域并改变之
senses.example: Cheap sensors became invasive in daily life before any rule was written.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价传感器在任何人写规则之前就已经侵入日常生活。
senses.why: Tools spread the way organisms do, into spaces nobody assigned them, and the metaphor carries over.
senses.whyCN: 工具扩散的方式像生物一样，进入没人分给它们的空间，这个比喻因此顺手可用。

senses.title: A noun use for such organisms
senses.definition: in the plural, a shorthand for invasive plants or animals in management writing
senses.definitionCN: 在管理文本中以复数形式作为入侵植物或动物的简称
senses.example: The crew spent the summer pulling invasives from the channel.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班组花了整个夏天从水道里拔除入侵物种。
senses.why: Field crews shorten long phrases, so the adjective became a plural noun meaning the plants and animals they pull.
senses.whyCN: 野外班组会缩短长短语，于是这个形容词成了复数名词，指他们拔除的动植物。

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle turned adjective: a prefix for into and a verb for going make the verb to invade, and an adjective ending makes the description.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语分词转成的形容词：表示「进入」的前缀与表示「走」的动词构成「侵入」，再加形容词词尾成为描述词。

items.en: Vadere meant to go or to proceed, and it supplied the movement at the heart of the word.
items.cn: 这个词意为走、前行，提供了词的核心动作。

items.en: The compound meant to go into, enter or attack, and it was used of armies and of disease.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为走进、进入、攻击，用于军队，也用于疾病。

items.en: The adjective meant given to entering or attacking, and Late Latin used it in medical writing.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为好进入、好攻击的，晚期拉丁语在医学写作中使用它。

items.en: French carried the adjective onward, and English took it in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词继续传下，英语在十七世纪借入。

items.en: Early English used it for armies and for arguments that encroached on another's ground.
items.cn: 早期英语用它指军队，也指侵占他人地盘的论点。

items.en: Ecologists applied it to organisms spreading beyond their native range with harmful effects; the usage settled in the later twentieth century.
items.cn: 生态学家把它用于越出原生范围扩散并造成有害影响的生物；这一用法在二十世纪后期稳定下来。

note.en: The first group shares the going-in stem; the second group separates invasion from mere foreign origin.
note.cn: 第一组共用「走入」词干；第二组把入侵与单纯的外来出身区分开。

entries.definition: To enter by force, of armies, diseases or organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 指以强力进入，用于军队、疾病或生物。

entries.definition: The act of entering by force, and the event ecology counts.
entries.definitionCN: 指强行进入的行为，也是生态学所计的事件。

entries.definition: One that enters by force.
entries.definitionCN: 指强行进入者。

entries.definition: The quality of spreading and entering, measured in risk screening.
entries.definitionCN: 指扩散与进入的性质，在风险筛查中被度量。

entries.definition: Tending to avoid or escape; it shares the going verb but with a prefix for out.
entries.definitionCN: 指倾向回避或逃开的；共用「走」动词，但前缀意为「向外」。

entries.definition: Present outside its native range, a statement about origin only.
entries.definitionCN: 指存在于原生范围之外，只陈述出身。

entries.definition: Brought by people from elsewhere, without any claim about harm.
entries.definitionCN: 指由人从别处带来，不含损害之意。

entries.definition: Advancing gradually into another's space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐侵占他人的空间或时间。

entries.definition: Pushing in where not wanted, common for privacy and devices.
entries.definitionCN: 指进入不受欢迎之处，常用于隐私与器械。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the going-in verb, the medical setting and the ecology test that separates origin from behaviour.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「走入」动词、医学场景，以及把出身与行为分开的生态学检验。

normal.en: Invade is go into, and invasive is the adjective of that going in.
normal.cn: 动词意为「走进去」，形容词就是这种进入的性质。

normal.en: Medicine asks how far the entry goes: open, minimally invasive, or no entry at all.
normal.cn: 医学问的是进入多深：开刀、微创，还是完全不进入。

normal.en: Alien and non-native state origin; invasive states behaviour and harm.
normal.cn: 「外来」陈述出身，「入侵性」陈述行为与损害。

normal.en: A naturalised poppy that stays in its field is not invasive, which is the commonest mistake.
normal.cn: 安分待在田里的归化罂粟不是入侵性的，这是最常见的错误。

normal.en: Minimally invasive is the fixed phrase that keeps the medical sense alive in everyday speech.
normal.cn: 「微创」是让医学义在日常语言里存活的固定说法。

abstract.en: Invasion is a claim about a boundary: the same movement is exploration in one frame and intrusion in another.
abstract.cn: 入侵是关于边界的判断：同样的移动，在一个框架里是探索，在另一个里是侵入。

abstract.en: Nature has no passports; the label is applied by the systems that receive the newcomer and pay for it.
abstract.cn: 自然界没有护照；这个标签由接收新来者并为之付出代价的那些系统贴上。

abstract.en: In medicine the word measures penetration of a body, in ecology penetration of a community: the geometry is the same.
abstract.cn: 医学上它度量对身体穿透，生态学上度量对群落的穿透：几何形状是一样的。

examples.en: The council removed the invasive shrub from the dune system.
examples.cn: 委员会清除了沙丘系统中的这种入侵灌木。

examples.en: Surgeons now prefer the less invasive route through the wrist.
examples.cn: 外科医生现在更青睐经手腕的侵入性较小的路径。

examples.en: Residents objected to the invasive questions at the checkpoint.
examples.cn: 居民反对检查站那些侵犯个人隐私的提问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因维西夫」——因是进来，维西夫是走，走进别人的地盘还不走，就是入侵性的

root: 拉丁语 vadere「走」→ invadere「走入、攻击」← in-「进入」→ 晚期拉丁语 invasivus「好进入的」→ 法语 invasif → 英语十七世纪借入。二十世纪后期生态学用它指越出原生范围扩散并造成损害的外来生物，此前主要指军事与医学上的侵入。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one movement of going in: the ecological spread, the origin test it is not, three kinds of physical entry, plants, armies, technology and a shorthand noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟随同一个「走入」的动作：生态扩散、它并不等同于的出身检验、三种实体进入、植物、军队、技术与名词简称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foreign vine sheets the bank, cutting light from the reeds below while its tips reach the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条外来藤蔓铺满堤岸，把下面的芦苇遮死，藤尖还探向水面。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGICAL SPREAD: a species taking ground, and a plant growing strongly enough to displace others.
branches.cn: 生态扩散：物种夺取地面，以及植物长到足以挤走其他植物。

branches.en: THE TEST IT IS NOT: foreign origin alone, which introduced and naturalised species also have.
branches.cn: 它并不等同的检验：单纯的外来出身，引入与归化物种同样具备。

branches.en: THE MEDICAL ENTRY: a procedure entering the body, and a growth crossing into tissue.
branches.cn: 医学进入：操作进入体内，以及生长越入组织。

branches.en: THE OTHER INTRUSIONS: privacy, armed force, and tools spreading into unexpected domains.
branches.cn: 其他侵入：隐私、武力，以及扩散到意外领域的工具。

branches.en: THE SHORTHAND: invasives as the working noun of removal crews.
branches.cn: 简称：清除班组日常工作用语中的「入侵物种」。

intro.en: A prefix for into and a verb for going make the verb, and an adjective ending makes the description.
intro.cn: 表示「进入」的前缀与表示「走」的动词构成动词，形容词词尾构成描述词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vadere, invadere, invasio and invasivus; the recorded chain runs without gaps.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「走」「走入」「进入」与「好进入的」等形式，有记录的链条中间没有断口。

items.example: It marks movement across a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 它标记越过边界的移动。

items.example: It supplies the movement in the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供词中的动作。

items.example: It is the recorded source of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是动词有记录的来源。

items.example: It is the recorded source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是形容词有记录的来源。

items.example: It turns the participle into a description.
items.exampleCN: 它把分词变成描述词。

items.example: It makes the noun for the entry.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示进入的名词。

items.example: It names the one entering.
items.exampleCN: 它命名进入的那一方。

items.example: It names the quality measured in screening.
items.exampleCN: 它命名筛查中所度量的性质。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from in- and vadere

derivatives.zh: 由该前缀加表示「走」的词干构成，义为「侵入」
由该动词加动作名词词尾构成，义为「入侵」
由该动词加施动名词词尾构成，义为「入侵者」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「非侵入性的」

definition_zh: 外来入侵物种；在原生范围之外定居、扩散并造成损害的物种
definition_en: a species introduced outside its native range that establishes, spreads and causes harm to ecosystems, economies or health
core_image: 一片浅水湿地被外来的螺铺满，本地水草只剩空茎，螺壳一直堆到泥岸上
scene: 湿地里一种外来的螺把本地水草啃光，还把寄生虫带给在这里越冬的水鸟。The lake manager listed the snail as an invasive species once it covered the delta.
sceneCN: 这里指在原生范围外定居、扩散并造成损害的物种（第 1 个义项：造成损害的外来定居种）；句意为这种螺铺满三角洲后，湖泊管理者把它列为外来入侵物种。

pos.zh: 外来入侵物种（可数短语名词，单复数同形）

derivatives.zh: 该短语的限定词，由拉丁语表示「走入」的动词派生，义为「侵入的；扩散成害的」
由该形容词的动词基座加动作名词词尾构成，义为「入侵」
由该动词加施动名词词尾构成，义为「入侵者」
该短语在政策文本中更完整的形式，义为「外来入侵物种」，强调外来出身
由否定前缀加该形容词与「物种」构成，义为「非入侵性物种」
相邻术语，指已定居但未造成明显损害的引入种，义为「归化物种」

senses.title: A species that spreads and causes harm
senses.titleCN: 扩散并造成损害的物种
senses.definition: a species that, once introduced outside its native range, spreads and damages the systems it enters
senses.definitionCN: 被引入原生范围之外后扩散开来、并损害所在系统的物种
senses.example: The grass became an invasive species because it outgrew every native seedling.
senses.exampleCN: 这种草之所以成为外来入侵物种，是因为它把本地每一株幼苗都压了下去。
senses.why: The phrase joins an adjective of forced entry to a word for kind, so it names a kind that takes ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示「强行进入」的形容词接到表示「种类」的词上，因此命名的是夺取地面的那一类。

senses.title: The four tests of introduction, establishment, spread and impact
senses.titleCN: 引入、定居、扩散、影响四项要件
senses.definition: a species meeting all four conditions, since a newcomer that stays put and harms nothing is not counted
senses.definitionCN: 同时满足四项条件的物种，因为定居而不造成损害的新来者并不计入
senses.example: Biologists ask four questions before calling a plant an invasive species.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家在把一种植物称为外来入侵物种之前，会先问四个问题。
senses.why: A definition that only says foreign would be useless to managers, so four observable conditions were written into it.
senses.whyCN: 只写「外来」的定义对管理者无用，因此写进了四个可观察的条件。

senses.title: The policy term of international agreements
senses.titleCN: 国际协定中的政策术语
senses.definition: the working term used in treaties and national strategies, often in the longer form invasive alien species
senses.definitionCN: 条约与国家战略中使用的作业术语，常以更完整的形式「外来入侵物种」出现
senses.example: The strategy sets a target for reducing invasive species by half.
senses.exampleCN: 这项战略设定了把外来入侵物种减少一半的目标。
senses.why: Treaties need a term that can be counted and reported, and the phrase supplied one.
senses.whyCN: 条约需要一个能计数、能报告的词，这个短语正好提供了。

senses.title: The routes by which they arrive
senses.definition: the pathways of arrival, such as ballast water, hull fouling, plant trade, pets and timber
senses.definitionCN: 抵达的途径，如压舱水、船体附着、植物贸易、宠物与木材
senses.example: Ballast water is the main route by which an invasive species reaches this bay.
senses.exampleCN: 压舱水是外来入侵物种抵达这片海湾的主要途径。
senses.why: Management begins at the door, so the word is used for the pathways as well as for the organisms.
senses.whyCN: 管理从门口开始，因此这个词也用于传入途径，而不只用于生物本身。

senses.title: The mechanisms of harm
senses.definition: competition, predation, hybridisation, disease transfer and altered fire or water regimes
senses.definitionCN: 竞争、捕食、杂交、疾病传播，以及改变的火情或水文情势
senses.example: The frog is an invasive species here partly because it carries a fungus lethal to local amphibians.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蛙在这里成为外来入侵物种，部分原因是它携带一种对本地两栖类致命的真菌。
senses.why: Harm has to be explained before it can be predicted, so the mechanisms entered the term's working use.
senses.whyCN: 损害必须先被解释才能预测，因此机制进入了这个术语的实际用法。

senses.title: The object of prevention and control
senses.definition: a target of border checks, early detection, eradication and long-term containment
senses.definitionCN: 边境检查、早期发现、根除与长期围控的对象
senses.example: Customs officers screen fruit for one high-risk invasive species at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 海关人员逐批检查水果，针对一种高风险的入侵物种。
senses.why: Once something is named it can be targeted, and the phrase moved into the language of operations.
senses.whyCN: 事物一旦被命名就可以被瞄准，这个短语于是进入了行动语言。

senses.title: Not every introduced species qualifies
senses.titleCN: 并非每个引入种都够格
senses.definition: a distinction from introduced and naturalised species, which arrived with people but cause no measured harm
senses.definitionCN: 与引入种和归化种相区别，后者随人而来，却没有测得的损害
senses.example: The daisy came with settlers yet is not an invasive species here.
senses.exampleCN: 这种雏菊随定居者而来，在这里却不算外来入侵物种。
senses.why: A label that fits every newcomer would lose its force, so harmless settlers were placed outside it.
senses.whyCN: 标签若适用于每个新来者就会失去力量，因此无害的定居者被排除在外。

senses.title: A threat concentrated on islands and closed waters
senses.titleCN: 集中于海岛与封闭水体的威胁
senses.definition: a risk that rises where native species evolved without the newcomer and lose their defences
senses.definitionCN: 在本地物种未曾与来者共同演化、因而失去防御力的地方，风险更高
senses.example: On this island the rat is the worst invasive species on record.
senses.exampleCN: 在这座岛上，鼠是有记录以来最严重的外来入侵物种。
senses.why: Isolation removes the defences that coevolution builds, so the same species does more damage there.
senses.whyCN: 隔离去掉了协同演化建立的防御，因此同一物种在那里造成更大损害。

senses.title: A cost carried by economies
senses.definition: an expense counted in crop losses, infrastructure damage, health care and control budgets
senses.definitionCN: 以作物损失、设施损坏、医疗支出与控制预算计算的开支
senses.example: The state counts the invasive species in its waters as a fishing loss.
senses.exampleCN: 该州把水域中的外来入侵物种计为渔业损失。
senses.why: Budgets require a category, and the phrase became one line item among many.
senses.whyCN: 预算需要一个科目，这个短语于是成了众多条目中的一行。

intro.en: The phrase is two Latin borrowings: an adjective built on the verb to go into, and a noun for kind or appearance. Ecology attached the adjective to the noun only in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁语借词组成：一个建立在「走入」动词上的形容词，一个表示「种类、外观」的名词。生态学把两者接在一起是二十世纪的事。

items.en: Vadere meant to go, and it supplied the movement inside the word for entering.
items.cn: 这个词意为走，提供了「进入」一词内部的运动。

items.en: The compound meant to go into or attack, and Late Latin made an adjective from it.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为走入、攻击，晚期拉丁语由它造出形容词。

items.en: The adjective meant given to entering, and it reached English through French.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为好进入的，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Species meant appearance, form or kind, and English took it unchanged as the biological word for a kind.
items.cn: 这个词意为外观、形态或种类，英语原样借入，用作表示生物一类的术语。

items.en: Both words were in English long before they were joined; the adjective described armies and diseases.
items.cn: 两个词早已在英语中，远在它们被接合之前；形容词那时描述军队与疾病。

items.en: The full phrase became standard in conservation writing in the later twentieth century, and treaties made it a legal term.
items.cn: 这个完整短语在二十世纪后期的保护文献中成为标准说法，条约又使它成为法律术语。

note.en: The first group shares invasive or species; the second group separates the term from mere foreign origin and from the harm it causes.
note.cn: 第一组共用 invasive 或 species；第二组把这个术语与单纯外来出身以及它造成的损害区分开。

entries.definition: The adjective: entering, spreading and causing harm.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：进入、扩散并造成损害。

entries.definition: The event of entering by force, which ecology counts.
entries.definitionCN: 指强行进入的事件，生态学对此计数。

entries.definition: A kind of organism, spelled alike in singular and plural.
entries.definitionCN: 指一类生物，单复数拼写相同。

entries.definition: A single example taken for study.
entries.definitionCN: 指取来研究的单个标本。

entries.definition: Tending to avoid; the going verb with a prefix for out.
entries.definitionCN: 指倾向回避；共用「走」动词，但前缀意为「向外」。

entries.definition: A species present outside its native range, a statement about origin only.
entries.definitionCN: 指存在于原生范围之外的物种，只陈述出身。

entries.definition: Brought by people from elsewhere, with no claim about harm.
entries.definitionCN: 指由人从别处带来，不含损害之意。

entries.definition: An introduced species that has settled and reproduces without spreading harmfully.
entries.definitionCN: 指已定居并能繁殖、但未有害扩散的引入种。

entries.definition: A species that damages crops or property, whether native or not.
entries.definitionCN: 指损害作物或财物的物种，不论是否本地产。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the four tests, the origin trap and the island case.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用四项要件、外来出身的陷阱与海岛情形。

normal.en: Four tests: brought in, settles, spreads, harms. Miss one and the label does not apply.
normal.cn: 四项要件：被带入、能定居、会扩散、造成损害。少一项这个标签就不适用。

normal.en: Alien, non-native and naturalised describe origin and status; only invasive describes the harm.
normal.cn: 「外来」「非原生」「归化」描述出身与状态，只有「入侵性」描述损害。

normal.en: Ballast water is the classic route: a ship empties a distant harbour into a new one.
normal.cn: 压舱水是典型途径：船把远方港口的生物倒进新港口。

normal.en: Islands are the worst case, because native species there never met the newcomer.
normal.cn: 海岛是最糟的情形，因为那里的原生种从未与来者相遇。

normal.en: Species is the same in the singular and the plural, so the phrase never needs an s.
normal.cn: 「物种」一词单复数同形，因此这个短语在复数时不必改变词形。

abstract.en: An invasive species is a traveller that succeeds too well, and success is measured by what it replaces.
abstract.cn: 外来入侵物种是一个成功过头的旅居者，而成功由它替换掉的东西来度量。

abstract.en: The label is a verdict on damage, not on travel; movement itself is ancient and blameless.
abstract.cn: 这个标签是对损害的判决，而不是对旅行的判决；移动本身古老而无罪。

abstract.en: Every port is a door, and the phrase is the name of what walked through without being checked.
abstract.cn: 每个港口都是一扇门，这个短语就是未经检查走过的那件东西的名字。

examples.en: The waterway is now choked by an invasive species of weed.
examples.cn: 这条水道现在被一种外来入侵水草堵塞。

examples.en: Climate change helps an invasive species move uphill faster.
examples.cn: 气候变化帮助外来入侵物种更快地向山上移动。

examples.en: The plan budgets more for prevention than for invasive species control.
examples.cn: 该方案为预防拨的款比入侵物种控制更多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因维西夫 斯比西兹」——前半是闯进来，后半是种类，闯进来还赖着不走的种类，就是外来入侵物种

root: 拉丁语 vadere「走」→ invadere「走入、攻击」→ 晚期拉丁语 invasivus → 法语 invasif → 英语的形容词；拉丁语 species「外观、种类」← specere「看」。两词二十世纪后期在保护文献中组合为固定术语，条约使其成为法律用语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses ring the term: the definition, its four tests, its policy life, its routes, its mechanisms, its management, the species that fall outside it, islands and money.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围住这个术语：定义、四项要件、政策生命、传入途径、损害机制、管理、被排除在外的物种、海岛与金钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shallow wetland paved with foreign snails, native weed stems stripped bare.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片被外来螺铺满的浅水湿地，本地水草的茎被啃得只剩空壳。

branches.en: THE DEFINITION: harm after spread, and the four conditions that must all hold.
branches.cn: 定义：扩散之后的损害，以及必须同时成立的四项条件。

branches.en: THE PAPER LIFE: a working term in treaties and national strategies.
branches.cn: 纸面生命：条约与国家战略中的作业术语。

branches.en: THE MECHANISM: how it arrives, and how it does damage once established.
branches.cn: 机制：它如何抵达，以及定居之后如何造成损害。

branches.en: THE RESPONSE AND THE BILL: prevention, eradication, control, and the cost in budgets.
branches.cn: 应对与账单：预防、根除、控制，以及预算上的开支。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDERS AND THE VULNERABLE GROUND: harmless naturalised species, and islands that cannot defend themselves.
branches.cn: 外界与脆弱地面：无害的归化种，以及无法自卫的海岛。

intro.en: One Latin going-in adjective and one Latin kind noun make the phrase, and both halves still build families.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「走入」形容词与一个拉丁语「种类」名词构成这个短语，两半至今都在造词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vadere, invadere, invasivus and species; every form below is recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「走」「走入」「好进入的」与「种类」，下列每个形式都有记录。

由该动词加动作名词词尾构成，义为「入侵」
