definition_zh: 食物链；生物之间谁吃谁的线性传递序列
definition_en: a single linear sequence of organisms in which each is eaten by the next, tracing the transfer of energy from producer to consumer
core_image: 一幅直排的图：水下藻类在最下层，小虾在其上，鱼再上一层，最后是一只俯冲的鹭
scene: 同一片水塘里，藻类被小虾吃，小虾被鱼吃，鱼又被岸边的鹭叼走。The pond's food chain runs from algae through shrimp and fish to the heron.
sceneCN: 这里指谁吃谁的单线传递序列（第 1 个义项：线性的取食与能量序列）；句意为这片水塘的食物链从藻类经小虾与鱼直到鹭。

pos.zh: 食物链（可数短语名词）
某一特定取食序列（用于生态学与教学）

derivatives.zh: 该短语的前半，源自古英语表示食物的词，义为「食物」
该短语的后半，源自拉丁语表示锁链的词，义为「链」
由该短语与表示「网」的词构成的相邻术语，义为「食物网」，指多条链交织成的网络
相关术语，由希腊语表示「营养」的词构成，义为「营养级」，指链上的位置
早期同义术语，义为「食物循环」，强调物质回流而非单线传递
由该后半与表示「长度」的词构成，义为「链长」，指链上环节数目

senses.title: A linear sequence of who eats whom
senses.definition: a single ordered line of organisms in which each is eaten by the one above it
senses.definitionCN: 一条有次序的单线，其中每一种生物都被上一层的那一种吃掉
senses.example: A food chain from pondweed to heron has only four links here.
senses.exampleCN: 这里从池草到鹭的一条食物链只有四个环节。
senses.why: The second word is a chain, and a chain has links in order, which is exactly what a sequence of eaters is.
senses.whyCN: 后半的意思是锁链，而锁链是有次序的环节，这正是「一连串取食者」的样子。

senses.title: Energy passing from producer to consumer
senses.titleCN: 能量从生产者向消费者的传递
senses.definition: the route by which captured energy moves from plants to herbivores and then to predators
senses.definitionCN: 被固定的能量从植物到植食者、再到捕食者的移动路线
senses.example: Every food chain begins with a plant or an alga that captures sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 每条食物链都始于固定阳光的植物或藻类。
senses.why: A chain of eaters is also a chain of transfers, so the term widened from bodies to the energy inside them.
senses.whyCN: 一连串取食者也是一连串转移，因此这个词从身体扩展到了身体里的能量。

senses.title: The three positions of producer, consumer and decomposer
senses.titleCN: 生产者、消费者与分解者的三个位置
senses.definition: the standard three-part division of roles along the sequence, with decomposers closing the loop
senses.definitionCN: 沿这条序列划分的标准三种角色，分解者负责把环闭上
senses.example: A food chain in a log has a fungus where a pond has a fish.
senses.exampleCN: 木头里的一条食物链，用真菌占用了池塘里鱼的位置。
senses.why: Three jobs are enough to describe any sequence, so the term took the standard three-part division.
senses.whyCN: 三种角色足以描述任何序列，因此这个词采用了标准的三分法。

senses.title: A length limited by energy loss
senses.titleCN: 受能量损耗限制的长度
senses.definition: a sequence that rarely exceeds four or five links because most energy is lost at each step
senses.definitionCN: 很少超过四五个环节的序列，因为每一步都会损失大部分能量
senses.example: No food chain in this lake is longer than five links.
senses.exampleCN: 这个湖里没有一条食物链超过五个环节。
senses.why: The tenth rule makes long chains impossible, and the limit itself became part of what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 「一成」规则使长链不可能，而这一限度本身也成了这个词描述的内容。

senses.title: A simplified model of a food web
senses.definition: an abstraction taken out of a network so that one pathway can be taught or measured
senses.definitionCN: 从网络中抽出的一条路径，以便教学或测量
senses.example: A textbook food chain hides the fact that the fish also eats insects.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书里的一条食物链掩盖了鱼也吃昆虫这一事实。
senses.why: Teaching needs a single line, so a path is cut out of the network and given the name of the whole.
senses.whyCN: 教学需要一条单线，于是从网络中切出一条路径，并冠以整体的名字。

senses.title: Grazing and detrital chains
senses.definition: two kinds of chain, one starting from living plants and one from dead matter and its microbes
senses.definitionCN: 两种链，一种始于活植物，一种始于死有机质及其微生物
senses.example: The detrital food chain in the marsh starts with fallen reed litter.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沼泽的碎屑食物链从落下的芦苇枯叶开始。
senses.why: Dead matter supports a sequence of its own, and the term had to cover both starting points.
senses.whyCN: 死有机质支撑着它自己的序列，这个词必须覆盖两种起点。

senses.title: A route for accumulating toxins
senses.definition: a pathway along which fat-soluble substances build up in ever higher concentrations
senses.definitionCN: 脂溶性物质在其中以越来越高浓度积累的路径
senses.example: Mercury climbs the food chain until top predators carry the heaviest load.
senses.exampleCN: 汞沿食物链上行，直到顶级捕食者携带最重的负担。
senses.why: Fat-soluble substances do not leave a body easily, so the sequence became the route of their concentration.
senses.whyCN: 脂溶性物质不易排出体外，这条序列于是成了它们浓缩的路线。

senses.title: The top predator at the end
senses.definition: the final position, occupied by a predator that is eaten by few or none
senses.definitionCN: 最后一个位置，由很少被吃或不被吃的捕食者占据
senses.example: The eagle sits at the top of this food chain and accumulates everything below it.
senses.exampleCN: 鹰坐在这条食物链的顶端，把下面的一切都累积在身上。
senses.why: Every line has an end, and the end is where fewest eaters remain.
senses.whyCN: 每条线都有末端，而末端正是取食者最少的地方。

senses.title: A chain that can be broken
senses.definition: a sequence that collapses when one link is removed, with effects passing down the line
senses.definitionCN: 某一环被移除时会断裂、并使影响沿线下传的序列
senses.example: Draining the pond broke the food chain at its second link.
senses.exampleCN: 排干池塘，把这条食物链在第二个环节处打断了。
senses.why: A chain is only as strong as its links, so the word began to be used for the event of losing one.
senses.whyCN: 链的强度取决于环扣，于是这个词开始用于「失去一环」这件事。

intro.en: Both words are old English nouns. Food is native Germanic and chain came from Latin through French; the compound is a twentieth-century ecology term.
intro.cn: 两个词都是古老的英语名词：前半「食物」属日耳曼本族词，后半「链」经法语来自拉丁语；这一复合词是二十世纪的生态学术语。

items.en: Foda meant food or nourishment, and it is related to the verb for feeding.
items.cn: 这个词意为食物、养料，与表示「喂养」的动词同源。

items.en: Catena meant a chain, and it named a series of linked rings.
items.cn: 这个词意为锁链，指一串相连的环节。

items.en: French carried the noun into English, where chain already meant linked metal and then any linked series.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带入英语，链在英语中先指相连的金属，后指任何相连的系列。

items.en: Animal ecology fixed the compound for a sequence of eaters in the nineteen twenties.
items.cn: 动物生态学在二十世纪二十年代把这个复合词固定为「一连串取食者」的意思。

items.en: Ecologists later stressed that a chain is a simplification cut from a web, and the term kept both uses.
items.cn: 生态学家后来强调链是从网中切出的简化，这个术语同时保留两种用法。

note.en: The first group shares food or chain; the second group is the network and the position vocabulary that surrounds the term.
note.cn: 第一组共用 food 或 chain；第二组是围绕这个术语的网络与位置词汇。

entries.definition: Nourishment taken by an organism, the first element.
entries.definitionCN: 指生物摄取的养料，是前半部分。

entries.definition: A series of linked parts, the second element.
entries.definitionCN: 指一串相连的部分，是后半部分。

entries.definition: The network the chain is cut from.
entries.definitionCN: 指链所从属的网络。

entries.definition: A linked record of handling; the same chain word in law.
entries.definitionCN: 指一串交接记录；同一个「链」字用于法律。

entries.definition: A connected series of vehicles; close in image but a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 指相连的车列；意象相近，但属另一个词。

entries.definition: The full network of feeding links, of which a chain is one path.
entries.definitionCN: 指取食关系的完整网络，链是其中一条路径。

entries.definition: A position on the chain, counted in feeding steps.
entries.definitionCN: 指链上的位置，按取食步数计算。

entries.definition: The movement of captured energy through a system, of which the chain is one route.
entries.definitionCN: 指被固定能量在系统中的移动，链是其中一条路线。

entries.definition: An older term stressing the return of matter rather than a one-way line.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的术语，强调物质回流而不是单向线路。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the linked-ring image, the energy rule and the difference from a web.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「相连环扣」的形象、能量规则以及与网的区别。

normal.en: A chain is rings in a row, which is why the term is linear and why it is a simplification.
normal.cn: 链是一排环扣，这正是这个术语线性、也正是它简化之处。

normal.en: Each step loses most of the energy, so no chain can be very long.
normal.cn: 每一步都损失大部分能量，所以链不可能很长。

normal.en: Food chain is one path; food web is all paths at once.
normal.cn: 食物链是一条路径，食物网是同时展开的所有路径。

normal.en: Top of the food chain is the everyday phrase for an apex predator.
normal.cn: 「食物链顶端」是顶级捕食者的日常说法。

normal.en: Grazing chains start from living plants, detrital chains from dead matter.
normal.cn: 牧食链始于活植物，碎屑链始于死有机质。

abstract.en: A chain is a story told as if there were only one plot, and ecology keeps the simplification because teaching needs a line.
abstract.cn: 链是假设只有一条情节的故事，生态学保留这种简化，因为教学需要一条线。

abstract.en: Energy moves up and matter goes round, and the chain shows only the first half of that double movement.
abstract.cn: 能量往上走，物质绕圈转，链只展示了这场双向运动的前一半。

abstract.en: The higher the link, the more concentrated the world becomes inside one body.
abstract.cn: 环节越高，世界在一个身体里就越浓缩。

examples.en: The food chain here begins with algae attached to the stones.
examples.cn: 这里的食物链始于附着在石头上的藻类。

examples.en: Removing the midge broke the food chain that fed the fish.
examples.cn: 移除这种摇蚊，打断了喂养鱼群的那条食物链。

examples.en: A short food chain loses less energy before reaching the predator.
examples.cn: 较短的食物链在到达捕食者之前损失的能量更少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「富德 拆恩」——富德是食物，拆恩是链子，把吃与被吃串成一条链子，就是食物链

root: 古英语 fōda「食物」；拉丁语 catena「锁链」→ 古法语 chaine → 英语中表示「链」的名词。两词在二十世纪二十年代的动物生态学中被固定为「一连串取食关系」的术语，后与表示网络的「食物网」相对。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep the line in view while changing what it carries: eaters, energy, roles, length, its status as a model, two kinds of chain, toxins, the apex and the break.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项守住这条线，只换它承载的东西：取食者、能量、角色、长度、作为模型的地位、两种链、毒素、顶端与断裂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vertical row from algae to shrimp to fish to a stooping heron.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅从藻类到小虾到鱼再到俯冲的鹭的竖排图。

branches.en: THE LINE AND ITS CARGO: a sequence of eaters, and the energy that travels along it.
branches.cn: 线与货物：取食者的序列，以及沿线旅行的能量。

branches.en: THE ROLES AND THE START: producer, consumer and decomposer, with grazing and detrital beginnings.
branches.cn: 角色与起点：生产者、消费者、分解者，以及牧食与碎屑两种起点。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: energy loss at each step caps the number of links.
branches.cn: 限度：每一步的能量损失给环节数上了限。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACTION: a single path cut out of a network for teaching or measurement.
branches.cn: 抽象：为教学或测量从网络中切出的单一路径。

branches.en: THE CONSEQUENCES: toxins concentrating upward, an apex at the end, and a line that snaps when a link is pulled.
branches.cn: 后果：向上浓缩的毒素、末端的顶级者，以及抽掉一环就会断的线。

intro.en: The first element is native Germanic and the second came through French from Latin, so the compound mixes two layers of English.
intro.cn: 前半是日耳曼本族词，后半经法语来自拉丁语，因此这个复合词混合了英语的两个层次。

latinIntro.en: Only the second element has a Latin source, recorded as catena and carried through French.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后半有拉丁语来源，有记录的形式为锁链一词，并经法语传来。

items.example: It names what is eaten.
items.exampleCN: 它命名被吃的东西。

items.example: It names the ordered connection.
items.exampleCN: 它命名有次序的连接。

items.example: It is the recorded source of the second element.
items.exampleCN: 它是后半部分有记录的来源。

items.example: It is the term the chain is contrasted with.
items.exampleCN: 它是与链相对的术语。

items.example: It names the position on the chain.
items.exampleCN: 它命名链上的位置。

items.example: It names the final position.
items.exampleCN: 它命名最末的位置。

items.example: It starts the detrital chain.
items.exampleCN: 它开启碎屑链。

items.meaning: build-up of a substance in a body
items.example: It travels along the chain.
items.exampleCN: 它沿链累积。

derivatives.zh: 由该短语换成表示「网」的后半构成，义为「食物网」
由该短语换成表示「循环」的后半构成，义为「食物循环」
由该后半与表示「长度」的词构成，义为「链长」
相关术语，义为「营养级」

definition_zh: 食物网；多条食物链交织成的取食关系网络
definition_en: the network formed when many feeding links among species are shown together, rather than one linear sequence
core_image: 同一片水塘的取食关系被画成一张网：藻类连向小虾与螺，鱼连向两者，鹭连向鱼与螺
scene: 同一片水塘里，鱼除了吃虾也吃水生昆虫，鹭既吃鱼也吃螺，关系被画成一张交叉的网。A food web shows all of these feeding links at once instead of one line.
sceneCN: 这里指多条取食关系交织成的网络（第 1 个义项：整体取食网络）；句意为食物网把这些取食关系一次性全部展示出来，而不是只画一条线。

pos.zh: 食物网（可数短语名词）
某一群落完整的取食关系网络

derivatives.zh: 该短语的前半，源自古英语表示食物的词，义为「食物」
该短语的后半，源自古英语表示织物的词，义为「网」
由该短语换成表示「链」的后半构成的相邻术语，义为「食物链」，指单条路径
由该短语与「模型」组合而成，义为「食物网模型」，指用于计算与预测的网络模型
食物网研究中的指标，由表示「连接」的词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「连接度」
食物网研究中的性质，由表示「杂食」的词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「杂食性」，指同时取食多个营养级

senses.title: A network of feeding links
senses.definition: the whole set of feeding links among the species of a community, shown as a network rather than a line
senses.definitionCN: 一个群落内全部取食关系的集合，以网络而非单线的形式呈现
senses.example: A food web for the estuary contains more than ninety species.
senses.exampleCN: 这片河口的食物网包含九十多个物种。
senses.why: Many chains share species, so a line cannot hold them and a net had to be named.
senses.whyCN: 多条链共享物种，一条线装不下，于是必须给一张网命名。

senses.title: Species as nodes and feeding as links
senses.titleCN: 物种为节点、取食为连线
senses.definition: a structure of nodes, usually species or populations, joined by directed links that record who eats whom
senses.definitionCN: 由节点（通常是物种或种群）与记录「谁吃谁」的有向连线构成的结构
senses.example: Each arrow in the food web points from the eaten to the eater.
senses.exampleCN: 食物网里的每个箭头都从被吃的一方指向取食的一方。
senses.why: A network needs points and connections before it can be counted, so species and meals became those two things.
senses.whyCN: 网络要有节点与连接才能计数，于是物种与取食成了那两样东西。

senses.title: A closer picture than the chain
senses.titleCN: 比食物链更接近真实的图景
senses.definition: a representation that keeps the alternative pathways and the omnivory a single chain must leave out
senses.definitionCN: 保留替代路径与杂食性的表示法，而单条链必须把这些略去
senses.example: The food web revealed that the fish also feeds on seeds.
senses.exampleCN: 这张食物网揭示出鱼也取食种子。
senses.why: Omnivory is common in the field, and a model that forbids it cannot describe a real community.
senses.whyCN: 杂食在野外很常见，禁止杂食的模型无法描述真实群落。

senses.title: Measured by connectance and link density
senses.titleCN: 以连接度与连接密度度量
senses.definition: a network summarised by how many links exist relative to the possible number, and by links per species
senses.definitionCN: 以实际连线相对于可能连线的比例、以及每个物种的连线数来概括的网络
senses.example: Two lakes with the same species differ in food web connectance.
senses.exampleCN: 两个物种相同的湖泊，在食物网连接度上并不相同。
senses.why: Two webs can look alike and behave differently, so ratios of links were invented to tell them apart.
senses.whyCN: 两张网可能看着相似却行为不同，于是发明了连线比例来区分。

senses.title: A framework for keystone effects
senses.definition: a structure in which the removal of one well-connected node propagates through many others
senses.definitionCN: 在其中移除一个连接众多的节点会波及许多其他节点的结构
senses.example: Removing the kelp took the food web apart from the bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 移除海藻，等于从底部把这食物网拆开。
senses.why: Effects travel along the arrows, and the network shows which arrows exist.
senses.whyCN: 影响沿箭头传播，而网络显示了哪些箭头存在。

senses.title: A tool for modelling and management
senses.definition: a quantitative object built into simulations used to predict the effects of fishing, planting or removal
senses.definitionCN: 被写入模拟以预测捕捞、种植或移除后果的定量对象
senses.example: Managers ran the food web model to test three fishing rules.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者运行食物网模型，检验三条捕捞规则。
senses.why: A picture is not a prediction, so the web was turned into numbers for simulation.
senses.whyCN: 图景不是预测，于是把网转成数字用于模拟。

senses.title: An indicator of stability
senses.definition: a network whose redundancy and weak links are read as measures of how far disturbance will spread
senses.definitionCN: 其冗余与弱连接被用来判断扰动会传播多远的网络
senses.example: A food web with many weak links absorbed the drought better.
senses.exampleCN: 一张弱连接众多的食物网更好地吸收了这次干旱。
senses.why: Redundancy decides how far a shock travels, and the web makes redundancy visible.
senses.whyCN: 冗余决定冲击传播多远，而网让冗余变得可见。

senses.title: Different webs in different habitats
senses.definition: a network differing between soil, fresh water and open sea, and including the microbial loop
senses.definitionCN: 在土壤、淡水与开阔海域各自不同，并包含微生物环的网络
senses.example: The soil food web is built on fungi and bacteria rather than on leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤食物网建立在真菌与细菌之上，而不是叶片之上。
senses.why: Soil and water are run by different organisms, so the same term had to be applied to unlike networks.
senses.whyCN: 土壤与水由不同生物运转，同一个术语因此被用到截然不同的网络上。

senses.title: Built from gut contents and isotopes
senses.titleCN: 由胃含物与同位素数据构建
senses.definition: a network estimated from what animals contain, what stable isotopes show and what field observation records
senses.definitionCN: 由动物体内残留、稳定同位素结果与野外观察记录估计出来的网络
senses.example: They rebuilt the food web after analysing the stomachs of forty fish.
senses.exampleCN: 他们分析了四十条鱼的胃之后重建了这张食物网。
senses.why: A web is an estimate assembled from evidence rather than an observed object, so its construction became part of its definition.
senses.whyCN: 网是由证据拼出的估计，而不是被观察的物体，因此构建方式成了定义的一部分。

intro.en: Food is a native Germanic noun and web is the old word for woven cloth. The compound applies the image of weaving to feeding, and became standard ecology in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: 前半「食物」是日耳曼本族名词，后半「网」是表示织物的古老词。这个复合词把「编织」的形象用到取食上，二十世纪成为生态学标准术语。

items.en: Foda meant food, related to the verb for feeding.
items.cn: 这个词意为食物，与表示「喂养」的动词同源。

items.en: Webb meant woven cloth, and it also named the spider's net.
items.cn: 这个词意为织物，也用来指蜘蛛的网。

items.en: Wefan meant to weave, and the noun kept the sense of threads crossing each other.
items.cn: 这个词意为编织，名词保留了「线彼此交叉」的意思。

items.en: A web of threads crossing in many directions is the opposite of a chain's single line, and the image needed no explanation.
items.cn: 一张向多方交叉的线网正好与链的单线相反，这个比喻无需解释。

items.en: Ecologists adopted the compound for the full set of feeding links in a community, and the phrase became standard after the nineteen twenties.
items.cn: 生态学家采用这个复合词表示一个群落全部取食关系，这个短语在二十世纪二十年代之后成为标准说法。

note.en: The first group shares food or web; the second group names the analytical quantities used to describe a network.
note.cn: 第一组共用 food 或 web；第二组是描述网络时所用的分析量。

entries.definition: Nourishment, the first element.
entries.definitionCN: 养料，是前半部分。

entries.definition: A woven network, the second element.
entries.definitionCN: 编织成的网，是后半部分。

entries.definition: A linked set of pages; the same web image in a different industry.
entries.definitionCN: 指相互链接的页面集合；同一个「网」的意象用于另一个行业。

entries.definition: A spider's net, the literal source of the image.
entries.definitionCN: 指蜘蛛网，是这一意象的字面来源。

entries.definition: To marry; historically related to pledging rather than weaving, a common false friend.
entries.definitionCN: 指结婚；历史上与「立誓」而非「编织」有关，是常见的误认同源。

entries.definition: One linear path through the network.
entries.definitionCN: 指网络中的一条线性路径。

entries.definition: A feeding position, a way of summarising nodes in a web.
entries.definitionCN: 指取食位置，是概括网中节点的一种方式。

entries.definition: The general mathematical object of nodes and links.
entries.definitionCN: 指由节点与连线构成的一般数学对象。

entries.definition: A simulation of a whole system, of which the food web is one part.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个系统的模拟，食物网是其中一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use weaving, the contrast with the chain, and the measurements ecologists take.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「编织」、与链的对照，以及生态学家所取的度量。

normal.en: Web says threads crossing in many directions, which is why it replaced the single line.
normal.cn: 「网」说的是向多方交叉的线，这正是它取代单线的原因。

normal.en: Nodes are species, arrows are meals: the whole picture is a map of eating.
normal.cn: 节点是物种，箭头是取食关系，整幅图就是一张取食地图。

normal.en: Connectance is links present divided by links possible.
normal.cn: 连接度等于已存在的连线除以可能存在的连线。

normal.en: Remove a well-connected node and the effect travels along many arrows at once.
normal.cn: 移除一个连接众多的节点，影响会沿许多箭头同时传播。

normal.en: The soil food web runs on fungi and bacteria, not on leaves.
normal.cn: 土壤食物网靠真菌与细菌运转，而不是靠叶片。

abstract.en: A web is a structure of dependencies, and its weakness is also its strength: many paths mean many routes for failure and for recovery.
abstract.cn: 网是一种依赖结构，它的弱点也是它的强处：多条路径既意味着多条失败的路线，也意味着多条恢复的路线。

abstract.en: The chain answers what eats what next; the web answers what happens if one thing stops.
abstract.cn: 链回答接下来谁吃谁，网回答如果某一样停下来会怎样。

abstract.en: Every arrow is a transfer of stored sunlight, and the web is the accounting of that light.
abstract.cn: 每个箭头都是一次储存阳光的转移，而网就是对这份阳光的核算。

examples.en: The food web of the marsh includes three species of snail.
examples.cn: 这片沼泽的食物网包含三种螺。

examples.en: Pesticides simplified the food web long before the birds declined.
examples.cn: 农药在鸟类数量下降之前很久就已简化了这张食物网。

examples.en: Researchers mapped the food web from stomach contents and isotope ratios.
examples.cn: 研究者根据胃含物与同位素比值绘制了食物网。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「富德 韦布」——富德是食物，韦布是织成的网，把吃与被吃织成一张网，就是食物网

root: 古英语 fōda「食物」；古英语 webb「织物、网」← wefan「编织」。两词在二十世纪生态学中组合为固定术语，表示一个群落全部取食关系，与单线的「食物链」相对。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses describe one network from several angles: its links, its nodes, its realism, its measurements, its keystone effects, its use in models, its stability, its habitats and how it is built.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从多个角度描述同一张网：连线、节点、真实性、度量、关键种效应、模型用途、稳定性、生境差异与构建方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pond's feeding relations drawn as crossing threads, algae to snail and shrimp, fish to both, heron to fish and snail.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片水塘的取食关系画成交叉的线，藻类连向螺与虾，鱼连向两者，鹭连向鱼与螺。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the whole set of links, with species as nodes and meals as arrows.
branches.cn: 对象：全部连线的集合，物种为节点，取食为箭头。

branches.en: THE REALISM: alternative pathways and omnivory that a single chain cannot hold.
branches.cn: 真实：单条链容纳不下的替代路径与杂食性。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: connectance and links per species, which let two webs be compared.
branches.cn: 度量：连接度与每物种连线数，使两张网可以比较。

branches.en: THE USE: keystone effects travelling through the network, and models used to test rules.
branches.cn: 用途：在网中传播的关键种效应，以及用来检验规则的模型。

branches.en: THE READING: stability from weak links, habitat-specific webs, and construction from guts and isotopes.
branches.cn: 读法：由弱连接看稳定性、各生境不同的网，以及由胃含物与同位素构建。

intro.en: Both elements are native English, so the compound is Germanic in build even though its science is modern.
intro.cn: 两个成分都是英语本族词，因此尽管这门科学是现代的，这个复合词的构造属日耳曼式。

latinIntro.en: Neither element has a Latin source, so the Latin entries are left empty rather than filled with approximations.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都没有拉丁语来源，因此拉丁语词条留空，而不是用近似形式填充。

items.example: It names what is eaten.
items.exampleCN: 它命名被吃的东西。

items.example: It names the crossing structure.
items.exampleCN: 它命名交叉的结构。

items.example: It is the recorded source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是该名词有记录的来源。

items.example: It is the structure the web replaces.
items.exampleCN: 它是被网取代的那种结构。

items.example: It names a species in the model.
items.exampleCN: 它命名模型中的一个物种。

items.example: It names a feeding relation.
items.exampleCN: 它命名一条取食关系。

items.meaning: the share of possible links that exist
items.meaningCN: 已存在连线占可能连线的比例
items.example: It is the standard network measure.
items.exampleCN: 它是标准网络度量。

items.meaning: the stone that holds an arch
items.example: It names a species whose removal collapses the structure.
items.exampleCN: 它命名移除后会使结构崩塌的物种。

derivatives.zh: 由该短语换成表示「链」的后半构成，义为「食物链」
由该短语与「模型」组合而成，义为「食物网模型」
由表示「连接」的词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「连接度」
由表示「杂食」的词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「杂食性」

definition_zh: 营养级；生物在取食序列中所处的层级位置
definition_en: the position an organism occupies in a feeding sequence, counted in steps from the primary producer
core_image: 一段被分成几层的阶梯：最下层是藻类，往上依次是小虾、鱼、鹭，每层都标着取食的步数
scene: 同一片水塘里，藻类站在最下面一级，小虾在它上面一级，鱼再上一级，鹭在最上面。Each species occupies a different trophic level according to what it eats.
sceneCN: 这里指按取食步数确定的位置（第 1 个义项：由取食步数决定的层级位置）；句意为每个物种依据所吃的东西处在不同的营养级。

pos.zh: 营养级（可数短语名词）
取食序列中的层级位置（用于能量与稳定性分析）

derivatives.zh: 该短语的限定词，源自希腊语表示「营养」的词，义为「营养的；取食的」
由该形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在营养层面上」
由该形容词与表示「级联」的词构成，义为「营养级联」，指跨级的连锁效应
由该形容词与表示「位置」的词构成，义为「营养位置」，是更精确的连续量
由表示「良好」的前缀加词根构成，义为「富营养的」，指养分过多的水体
由表示「稀少」的前缀加词根构成，义为「贫营养的」，指养分很少的水体

senses.title: A position counted in feeding steps
senses.titleCN: 按取食步数计算的位置
senses.definition: the number of steps by which an organism is removed from the primary producer in a feeding sequence
senses.definitionCN: 生物在取食序列中离初级生产者相隔的步数
senses.example: Algae sit at the first trophic level and the heron at the fourth.
senses.exampleCN: 藻类位于第一个营养级，鹭位于第四个。
senses.why: Counting steps is the only way to place an organism without listing its whole diet.
senses.whyCN: 数步数是把生物定位的唯一办法，不必列出它的全部食谱。

senses.title: The standard ladder of producers and consumers
senses.titleCN: 生产者与消费者的标准阶梯
senses.definition: the conventional rungs of producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers and so on
senses.definitionCN: 生产者、初级消费者、次级消费者等惯用层次
senses.example: Primary consumers form the second trophic level in every pond.
senses.exampleCN: 初级消费者在每一片水塘里都构成第二个营养级。
senses.why: Field guides needed fixed rungs, so the conventional order was written into the term.
senses.whyCN: 野外手册需要固定的层级，于是惯用次序被写进了术语。

senses.title: A position, not a species
senses.titleCN: 是位置而非物种的固定属性
senses.definition: a slot that one species can occupy differently depending on diet and life stage
senses.definitionCN: 一个可由同一物种依据食性与生活阶段而占据不同位置的槽位
senses.example: A fish can move between trophic levels as it grows.
senses.exampleCN: 一条鱼会随着长大在营养级之间移动。
senses.why: Diets change with age and season, so the position has to be able to move.
senses.whyCN: 食性随年龄与季节变化，这个位置必须能够移动。

senses.title: A continuous trophic position
senses.definition: a fractional value calculated from diet proportions instead of a whole rung
senses.definitionCN: 由食性比例算出的小数值，而不是整级
senses.example: The goby has a trophic level of two point seven.
senses.exampleCN: 这种虾虎鱼的营养级为二点七。
senses.why: Whole rungs hide mixed diets, so a fractional value was calculated to keep the proportion.
senses.whyCN: 整级掩盖了混合食谱，于是算出小数值以保留比例。

senses.title: Efficiency of transfer between rungs
senses.titleCN: 层与层之间的传递效率
senses.definition: the share of energy passed upward, commonly about a tenth at each step
senses.definitionCN: 向上传递的能量份额，通常每一步约为一成
senses.example: Only a small fraction of energy crosses from one trophic level to the next.
senses.exampleCN: 只有一小部分能量从一个营养级越过到下一个。
senses.why: Energy is lost as heat at every transfer, so the step between rungs became a measurable share.
senses.whyCN: 每次传递都有能量以热的形式损失，层间的这一步于是成了可度量的份额。

senses.title: The basis of trophic cascades
senses.definition: a ladder used to describe effects that skip down several rungs after a top predator changes
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述顶级捕食者改变后效应向下跳过数级的阶梯
senses.example: Wolves altered the whole trophic level structure of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 狼改变了整个谷地的营养级结构。
senses.why: A change at the top shows up several rungs below, and the ladder gave that spread a name.
senses.whyCN: 顶端的改变会显现在下面数层，阶梯给了这种传播一个名字。

senses.title: An index used in water assessment
senses.definition: a score computed from the proportions of organisms at different rungs to judge water quality
senses.definitionCN: 由不同层级生物比例算出、用以判断水质的分数
senses.example: The river's trophic level index rose after the sewage plant opened.
senses.exampleCN: 污水处理厂启用之后，这条河的营养级指数上升了。
senses.why: Water managers needed one number, so the proportions at each rung were folded into a score.
senses.whyCN: 水体管理者需要一个数字，于是各层比例被折叠成一个分数。

senses.title: The apex at the top rung
senses.definition: the highest occupied rung, held by predators that are rarely eaten
senses.definitionCN: 被占据的最高一层，由很少被吃的捕食者把持
senses.example: The shark stands at the highest trophic level in this bay.
senses.exampleCN: 在这片海湾里，鲨鱼站在最高的营养级。
senses.why: The top rung is defined by the absence of predators rather than by any trait of the animal.
senses.whyCN: 最高一层由「没有捕食者」而非动物的任何特征来定义。

senses.title: Rungs in detrital pathways
senses.definition: positions counted from dead matter rather than from living producers
senses.definitionCN: 从死有机质而非活生产者开始计算的位置
senses.example: In the detrital trophic level, the first step is fallen leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 在碎屑营养级路径中，第一步是落下的叶子。
senses.why: Dead matter feeds a sequence of its own, so the count had to start from litter as well as from leaves.
senses.whyCN: 死有机质喂养着它自己的序列，因此计数也必须从枯落物起算。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek adjective for nourishing to a Latin-derived word for a balance. The pairing is a twentieth-century ecology usage built on nineteenth-century energy studies.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊语表示「滋养」的形容词，接到一个源自拉丁语、意为「天平」的词上。这一配对是二十世纪生态学在十九世纪能量研究基础上建立的用法。

items.en: Trophe meant nourishment or food, and it supplied the adjective for what feeds.
items.cn: 这个词意为营养或食物，提供了表示「有营养的」的形容词。

items.en: Trephein meant to nourish or to raise, and it is the verb behind the noun.
items.cn: 这个词意为养育、养大，是名词背后的动词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology made the adjective for feeding and nutrition.
items.cn: 十九世纪的生理学造出这个表示取食与营养的形容词。

items.en: Libella meant a small balance or a level, a diminutive of the word for scales.
items.cn: 这个词意为小天平或水平仪，是表示「秤」的词的小称形式。

items.en: French carried the noun into English as level, meaning a flat position in a scale.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带入英语，意为刻度上的一个水平位置。

items.en: Energy studies of the nineteen forties fixed the phrase as a rung in a feeding ladder; the exact first use is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 二十世纪四十年代的能量研究把这个短语固定为取食阶梯上的一层；确切首见时间只能给约数。

note.en: The first group shares trophic or level; the second group names the quantities and structures built on the rung.
note.cn: 第一组共用 trophic 或 level；第二组是建立在这一层之上的量与结构。

entries.definition: Relating to feeding and nutrition, the first element.
entries.definitionCN: 指与取食和营养有关的，是前半部分。

entries.definition: At the level of feeding relations.
entries.definitionCN: 指在取食关系的层面上。

entries.definition: A flat position on a scale, the second element.
entries.definitionCN: 指刻度上的水平位置，是后半部分。

entries.definition: Rich in nutrients, built on the same feeding stem.
entries.definitionCN: 指养分丰富的，建立在同一个「营养」词干上。

entries.definition: A prize or memorial; it looks close but comes from a word for turning away.
entries.definitionCN: 指奖品或纪念物；形近，但出自表示「转开」的词。

entries.definition: The continuous version of the rung, calculated from diet proportions.
entries.definitionCN: 指这一层的连续形式，由食性比例算出。

entries.definition: The linear sequence on which the rungs are counted.
entries.definitionCN: 指计算层级所依据的线性序列。

entries.definition: The network in which rungs are not single positions but ranges.
entries.definitionCN: 指层级不是单一点而是范围的网络。

entries.definition: A stack showing the losses between rungs.
entries.definitionCN: 指展示层间损耗的堆叠图。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the feeding stem, the balance word and the tenth rule.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「营养」词干、「天平」一词与「一成」规则。

normal.en: Trophe is nourishment, so trophic means to do with feeding.
normal.cn: 词根意为营养，所以这个形容词意为与取食有关。

normal.en: The rungs are producer, first consumer, second consumer, and so on.
normal.cn: 层级依次是生产者、第一消费者、第二消费者，如此类推。

normal.en: A species is not nailed to a rung; a growing fish climbs.
normal.cn: 物种并不被钉在某一层；长大的鱼会往上爬。

normal.en: Roughly a tenth of the energy passes to the next rung, which caps the ladder's height.
normal.cn: 大约一成能量传到下一层，这给阶梯的高度设了上限。

normal.en: Level came from a small balance, so each rung is a weighing point.
normal.cn: 后半原指小天平，所以每一层都是一个称量点。

abstract.en: A trophic level is a coordinate, not an identity: it says where a body sits in the flow, not what it is.
abstract.cn: 营养级是一个坐标，不是身份：它说的是一个身体在能流中的位置，而不是它是什么。

abstract.en: Each step upward is a tax paid in energy, which is why the top of any ladder is thinly populated.
abstract.cn: 每向上一层都要用能量缴税，这就是任何阶梯顶端都稀疏的原因。

abstract.en: The same animal can be a predator in one calculation and prey in the next, so the rung is a relation rather than a rank.
abstract.cn: 同一只动物在一次计算里是捕食者，在下一次里是猎物，因此这一层是关系而不是等级。

examples.en: Grasshoppers feed at the second trophic level in this meadow.
examples.cn: 在这片草甸里，蝗虫在第二个营养级取食。

examples.en: Long-lived predators sit at a high trophic level and accumulate toxins.
examples.cn: 寿命长的捕食者处在高营养级，因而累积毒素。

examples.en: The study compared biomass across four trophic levels.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较了四个营养级上的生物量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「特罗菲克 莱沃」——特罗菲克是营养，莱沃是层级，按营养排出的层级就是营养级

root: 希腊语 trophē「营养」← trephein「养育」→ 英语中表示「营养的」形容词；拉丁语 libella「小天平」← libra「秤」→ 古法语 livel → 英语中表示「层级」的名词。二十世纪四十年代的能量研究把两者固定为取食阶梯的层级，确切首见时间只能给约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses hold one coordinate and vary what is counted: steps, the standard ladder, species versus position, fractional values, transfer efficiency, cascades, indices, the apex and detrital rungs.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项守住同一个坐标，只改变所数的东西：步数、标准阶梯、物种与位置的差别、连续数值、传递效率、级联、指数、顶端与碎屑路径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short ladder from algae through shrimp and fish to the heron, each step marked with a feeding count.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段从藻类经小虾、鱼到鹭的短阶梯，每一层都标着取食步数。

branches.en: THE LADDER: positions counted from the producer, in the conventional order.
branches.cn: 阶梯：从生产者起算的位置，按惯用顺序排列。

branches.en: THE SLOT: a position a species may occupy differently as it grows or changes diet.
branches.cn: 槽位：同一物种随生长或食性变化可能占据的不同位置。

branches.en: THE CONTINUOUS VALUE: a fractional position computed from diet proportions.
branches.cn: 连续值：由食性比例算出的分数位置。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNTING: a tenth passing upward, and indices used to judge water.
branches.cn: 核算：一成向上传递，以及用来判断水质的指数。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURES: cascades across rungs, an apex at the top, and rungs counted from dead matter.
branches.cn: 结构：跨层的级联、顶端的顶级者，以及从死有机质起算的层级。

intro.en: A Greek nourishment stem and a Latin balance word make the phrase, and both still generate vocabulary.
intro.cn: 希腊语「营养」词干与拉丁语「天平」词构成这个短语，两者至今都在生成词汇。

latinIntro.en: The first element is Greek, so Latin entries belong to the second half and to the derived scientific words.
latinIntro.cn: 前半是希腊语，因此拉丁语词条属于后半以及派生出的科学词。

items.example: It marks everything to do with feeding.
items.exampleCN: 它标记与取食有关的一切。

items.example: It makes the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词。

items.example: It is the recorded Greek source.
items.exampleCN: 它是有记录的希腊语来源。

items.example: It is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是名词背后的动词。

items.example: It is the recorded source of the second element.
items.exampleCN: 它是后半部分有记录的来源。

items.example: It is the base of the diminutive.
items.exampleCN: 它是小称形式的基座。

items.example: It forms the adjective of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成该名词的形容词。

items.example: It marks nutrient-rich water.
items.exampleCN: 它标记养分丰富的水体。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「营养的」
由该形容词与表示「级联」的词构成，义为「营养级联」
由表示「良好」的前缀加该词干构成，义为「富营养的」
由表示「稀少」的前缀加该词干构成，义为「贫营养的」

definition_zh: 承载力；环境在不被破坏的前提下能长期维持的最大种群数量
definition_en: the largest population of a species that an environment can sustain over the long term without degrading
core_image: 一片草场被分成几块，牧草的高度刚好能供一群羊吃到下一季，再多一群就会露出草根
scene: 这片草场每年只够养这么多羊，再多一群就会把草根啃光，下一季长不回来。The ranger kept the flock below the carrying capacity of the pasture.
sceneCN: 这里指环境在不被破坏时能长期维持的最大种群量（第 1 个义项：可持续的最大种群数量）；句意为护林员把羊群规模控制在草场承载力之下。

pos.zh: 承载力（不可数短语名词）
某环境对某种群的最大维持量

derivatives.zh: 该短语的前半，经法语源自拉丁语表示「装车」的词，义为「承载；运载」
该短语的后半，源自拉丁语表示「能容纳」的词，义为「容量；能力」
由该名词的拉丁词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「容量大的」
由表示「过度」的前缀加该名词构成，义为「产能过剩」，指超出可维持的量
相邻术语，指可长期持续收获的量，义为「可持续产量」
相邻术语，指在承载力上限下先快后慢、最终趋平的增长形式，义为「逻辑斯蒂增长」

senses.title: The largest sustainable population
senses.titleCN: 可长期维持的最大种群
senses.definition: the maximum number of individuals an area can support indefinitely without damaging the resources they depend on
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区在不损害其依赖的资源的前提下可以无限期支撑的最大个体数
senses.example: The island's carrying capacity for deer is about one herd.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛对鹿的承载力大约是一群。
senses.why: The phrase answers a practical question: how many can be kept without the place losing the ability to keep them.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语回答一个实际问题：能养多少而不让地方失去供养能力。

senses.title: The ceiling K in logistic growth
senses.titleCN: 逻辑斯蒂增长中的上限
senses.definition: the upper limit in the growth equation at which births and deaths balance
senses.definitionCN: 增长方程中出生与死亡相抵的上限值
senses.example: In the growth curve, the population levels off at carrying capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 在增长曲线上，种群在承载力处趋于平缓。
senses.why: Growth equations need a ceiling symbol, and the phrase supplied the meaning behind the letter.
senses.whyCN: 增长方程需要一个上限符号，这个短语提供了字母背后的含义。

senses.title: Determined by limiting resources
senses.definition: a ceiling set by whichever resource runs out first, such as food, water, shelter or nesting sites
senses.definitionCN: 由最先耗尽的资源决定的上限，如食物、水、隐蔽处或营巢地
senses.example: Nesting sites, not grass, set the carrying capacity for these terns.
senses.exampleCN: 对这些燕鸥来说，决定承载力的是营巢地，而不是草。
senses.why: A place fails at its weakest point, so the ceiling is set by one resource rather than by the total.
senses.whyCN: 地方在最弱处失效，因此上限由一个资源而非总量决定。

senses.title: Not a fixed number
senses.definition: a value that shifts with season, rainfall, disturbance and the species' own behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 随季节、降雨、扰动与物种自身行为而变的数值
senses.example: The carrying capacity of the range falls by half in a drought year.
senses.exampleCN: 在干旱年份，这片牧场的承载力会下降一半。
senses.why: Rain and season change supply, so a single number would be false precision.
senses.whyCN: 降雨与季节改变供给，单一数字只是虚假的精确。

senses.title: Overshoot and decline
senses.definition: a state in which numbers pass the ceiling, damage the resource and then fall sharply
senses.definitionCN: 数量越过上限、损坏资源、随后急剧下降的状态
senses.example: The flock overshot carrying capacity and crashed in the next winter.
senses.exampleCN: 羊群超过了承载力，在下一个冬天急剧减少。
senses.why: Numbers can pass the ceiling before damage shows, and that delay is what makes the crash sharp.
senses.whyCN: 数量可以在损害显现前越过上限，这种延迟使崩溃来得更急。

senses.title: A number used in wildlife management
senses.titleCN: 野生动物管理所用的数值
senses.definition: a figure used to set hunting quotas, stocking rates and culling targets
senses.definitionCN: 用来设定猎取配额、放养率与淘汰目标的数值
senses.example: The quota was set at a third of the estimated carrying capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 配额被定在估算承载力三分之一处。
senses.why: Managers need a fraction of the ceiling rather than the ceiling itself, because the resource must regrow.
senses.whyCN: 管理者需要的是上限的一部分而非上限本身，因为资源必须再生。

senses.title: A contested figure for human populations
senses.titleCN: 用于人类人口的争议数值
senses.definition: an estimate for how many people an area or the planet can support, disputed because needs and technology vary
senses.definitionCN: 对一片地区或整个星球能支撑多少人的估计，因需求与技术不同而有争议
senses.example: Debate over the human carrying capacity of the planet has run for two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 关于地球人类承载力的争论已经持续了两个世纪。
senses.why: People change their needs and their tools, so the same calculation gives widely different answers.
senses.whyCN: 人的需求与工具都会变，同一套算法会给出差别极大的答案。

senses.title: Related to sustainable yield
senses.definition: a ceiling from which the maximum harvest that can be taken each year is calculated
senses.definitionCN: 据此算出每年可获取的最大收获量的上限
senses.example: The fishing rule takes half the carrying capacity as sustainable yield.
senses.exampleCN: 这条捕捞规则把承载力的一半作为可持续产量。
senses.why: Harvest rules are derived from the ceiling, which links the concept to everyday quotas.
senses.whyCN: 收获规则由上限推出，这把概念与日常配额连在一起。

senses.title: A ceiling that technology can shift
senses.definition: a limit that moves when farming, storage, trade or energy use changes what the land can supply
senses.definitionCN: 当耕作、储存、贸易或能源使用改变土地供给能力时随之移动的上限
senses.example: Fertiliser raised the carrying capacity of the same fields.
senses.exampleCN: 化肥提高了同一片田地的承载力。
senses.why: Fertiliser and storage change what a hectare can supply, so the ceiling moves with technique.
senses.whyCN: 化肥与储存改变了每公顷的供给能力，因此上限随技术移动。

intro.en: The phrase joins a verb for bearing a load, which came through French from Latin, with a Latin noun for the ability to hold. Range managers used it for livestock before ecologists used it for populations.
intro.cn: 这个短语把经法语来自拉丁语、意为「承担负载」的动词，接到一个表示「容纳能力」的拉丁名词上。牧场管理者先把它用于牲畜，生态学家后来才用于种群。

items.en: The wagon word entered Latin from a Celtic source and named a four-wheeled vehicle.
items.cn: 这个表示车子的词从凯尔特语进入拉丁语，指四轮车。

items.en: The verb meant to load a wagon, and French carried it toward the English verb to carry.
items.cn: 这个动词意为装车，法语把它传向英语中表示「承载」的动词。

items.en: The verb meant to transport or bear, and English took it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 这个动词意为运送、承担，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: Capere meant to take or hold, and it produced the adjective for able to hold much.
items.cn: 这个词意为拿取、容纳，由其产生表示「能容纳很多」的形容词。

items.en: The noun meant capacity or the power to contain, and English borrowed it directly.
items.cn: 这个名词意为容量、容纳的能力，英语直接借入。

items.en: Stock raisers first used the phrase for the number of animals a pasture could bear, and population ecology took it up later; the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 畜牧者先把这个短语用于一片牧场能承担的牲畜数，种群生态学后来才采用；确切首见时间不确定。

note.en: The first group shares carry or capacity; the second group names the related ceilings and yields.
note.cn: 第一组共用 carry 或 capacity；第二组是相关的上限与产量说法。

entries.definition: To bear or transport a load, the first element.
entries.definitionCN: 指承负或运送，是前半部分。

entries.definition: The ability to contain, the second element.
entries.definitionCN: 指容纳的能力，是后半部分。

entries.definition: Roomy, able to hold much, from the same holding stem.
entries.definitionCN: 指宽敞、能装很多，出自同一「容纳」词干。

entries.definition: Able to do or hold, a close relative of capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 指有能力做或容纳，是「容量」的近亲。

entries.definition: Developing skills in an organisation; the same noun in a different field.
entries.definitionCN: 指在组织中培养能力；同一个名词用于另一领域。

entries.definition: The amount that can be harvested each year without reducing the stock.
entries.definitionCN: 指每年可收获而不减少存量的数量。

entries.definition: The range of conditions a species can survive, a physiological ceiling.
entries.definitionCN: 指物种能存活的条件范围，是生理上限。

entries.definition: Animals placed per unit area, the management number derived from the ceiling.
entries.definitionCN: 指单位面积放养的牲畜数，是由上限推出的管理数值。

entries.definition: The largest long-term harvest, often set at half the ceiling.
entries.definitionCN: 指最大的长期收获量，常定在上限的一半。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the wagon-load image, the shifting ceiling and the management use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「装车」的形象、会移动的上限与管理用途。

normal.en: Carry is load a wagon, capacity is how much it holds: the phrase is a wagon full of animals.
normal.cn: 前半是给车装货，后半是能装多少：整个短语就是一车装满的动物。

normal.en: K is the ceiling in the growth equation, where births equal deaths.
normal.cn: 方程里的上限符号代表出生与死亡相抵的那一点，在那里出生等于死亡。

normal.en: The first resource to run out sets the ceiling, and it is often nesting sites rather than food.
normal.cn: 最先耗尽的资源决定上限，而它常常是营巢地而不是食物。

normal.en: The number moves every season, so any figure should carry the year it was measured.
normal.cn: 数值每个季节都在动，因此任何数字都该注明测量年份。

normal.en: Management takes a fraction of the ceiling, because taking all of it leaves nothing to regrow.
normal.cn: 管理只取上限的一部分，因为全取走就没有可再生的了。

abstract.en: Carrying capacity is a promise made by a place about how much it can be asked to bear, and the asking is the variable.
abstract.cn: 承载力是一个地方就自己能被要求承担多少作出的承诺，而「要求」才是变量。

abstract.en: Overshoot is borrowing from the next season, and the debt is collected with interest.
abstract.cn: 超载是向下一季借债，而债是按复利收回的。

abstract.en: A ceiling is a relationship between needs and supplies, so it moves when either side moves.
abstract.cn: 上限是需求与供给之间的关系，因此任何一侧移动它都会移动。

examples.en: The park's carrying capacity for wolves was set at twelve packs.
examples.cn: 公园对狼的承载力被设定为十二群。

examples.en: Grazing above carrying capacity turned the meadow into bare ground.
examples.cn: 超过承载力的放牧把草甸变成了裸地。

examples.en: Researchers re-estimated carrying capacity after the rains failed.
examples.cn: 降雨失败之后，研究者重新估算了承载力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「开瑞英 卡帕西提」——前面是承载，后面是容量，一个地方能装下多少活物，就是它的承载力

root: 高卢语 carrus「四轮车」→ 拉丁语 carricare「装车」→ 法语 carier「运送、承担」→ 英语中表示「承载」的动词；拉丁语 capere「容纳、拿取」→ capacitas「容量」→ 英语中表示「容量」的名词。两词十九至二十世纪间合为牧场与种群管理的术语，确切首见时间不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one ceiling as it moves: the sustainable maximum, the K of a growth curve, the limiting resource, seasonal change, overshoot, management quotas, human debate, sustainable yield and technological shift.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一道天花板移动：可持续最大值、增长曲线中的上限、限制性资源、季节变化、超载、管理配额、人类争议、可持续产量与技术改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pasture grazed to the right height for one flock, with bare roots showing where a second flock would stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片被一群羊吃到恰当高度的草场，再多一群就会露出草根。

branches.en: THE CEILING: the sustainable maximum, and the K where births balance deaths.
branches.cn: 天花板：可持续的最大值，以及出生与死亡相抵的上限值。

branches.en: THE VARIABLES: the first resource to run out, and the seasons that move the number.
branches.cn: 变量：最先耗尽的资源，以及让数字移动的季节。

branches.en: THE CONSEQUENCE OF PASSING IT: damage, then a sharp fall.
branches.cn: 越界的后果：先是损坏，随后急剧下降。

branches.en: THE HARVEST RULE: quotas for hunting, and sustainable yield taken as a fraction.
branches.cn: 收获规则：狩猎配额，以及按比例取用的可持续产量。

branches.en: THE HUMAN AND TECHNICAL CASES: a disputed figure for people, and a ceiling that fertiliser can raise.
branches.cn: 人类与技术情形：用于人口的争议数值，以及化肥可以提高的上限。

intro.en: A Celtic wagon word reached Latin and became an English verb for bearing; a Latin holding verb became an English noun for capacity.
intro.cn: 凯尔特语的「车」词进入拉丁语，成为英语表示「承担」的动词；拉丁语表示「容纳」的动词成为英语表示「容量」的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies carrus, carricare, capere and capacitas; the Celtic origin of the wagon word is the usual attribution.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「车」「装车」「容纳」与「容量」；这个「车」词的凯尔特语来源属通行归属。

items.example: It names the load placed on a place.
items.exampleCN: 它命名加在地方上的负载。

items.example: It names how much can be held.
items.exampleCN: 它命名能装多少。

items.example: It is the recorded source of the carrying verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是「承载」动词有记录的来源。

items.example: It supplies the image of loading.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「装货」的形象。

items.example: It is the base of the capacity noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是「容量」名词的基座。

items.example: It is the adjective behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是名词背后的形容词。

items.example: It makes the abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成抽象名词。

items.example: It marks numbers beyond the ceiling.
items.exampleCN: 它标记越过上限的数量。

由该拉丁名词直接借入，义为「容量」
由该拉丁词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「容量大的」
由表示「过度」的前缀加该名词构成，义为「超出可维持的量」
